2025-10.name: Post-Disaster Assistance Online Accountability Act
2025-10.plain: The House voted 426 to 0 to pass a bill requiring federal agencies that give disaster aid to publish, every three months, how much aid they provided, how much was spent or committed, and what projects it went to, all in one public online location.

2025-100.name: Congressional Budget Framework for 2025 to 2034
2025-100.plain: The House voted 216 to 214 to accept the Senate's changes to a budget framework that sets federal spending, revenue and debt levels for 2025 through 2034 and directs House committees to prepare future deficit-changing legislation. The measure was passed by the House.

2025-101.name: SAVE Act: Motion to Recommit
2025-101.plain: The House voted on whether to send the SAVE Act back to committee instead of moving to a final vote. The motion failed, 211 to 215. The bill would require people to show documentary proof of U.S. citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections.

2025-102.name: SAVE Act (Proof of Citizenship to Register to Vote)
2025-102.plain: The House voted to pass the SAVE Act, 220 to 208. The bill would require people to show documentary proof of U.S. citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections, and would require states to remove noncitizens from their voter lists.

2025-103.name: Consumer Safety Standards for Lithium-Ion Batteries
2025-103.plain: The House voted 365 to 42 to pass a bill requiring the Consumer Product Safety Commission to issue a safety rule for lithium-ion batteries used in electric bikes and electric scooters. The rule would require makers and sellers to follow existing battery safety standards.

2025-104.name: TAKE IT DOWN Act
2025-104.plain: The House passed the TAKE IT DOWN Act, 409 to 2. It would make it a crime to publish intimate images of people without their consent, including computer-generated fakes, and would require websites and apps to remove such images within 48 hours of a request.

2025-105.name: Rule Providing for Consideration of Five Resolutions on Environmental Rules
2025-105.plain: The House voted 215 to 206 to end debate and move to a final vote on a procedural measure setting the terms for considering five resolutions that would overturn federal environmental rules, including ones on Glen Canyon motor vehicles, longfin smelt protection, and California vehicle emission standards.

2025-106.name: Debate Rules for Five Environmental Disapproval Resolutions
2025-106.plain: The House approved the rules for debating five resolutions that would overturn federal environmental regulations, including California vehicle emission standards and a protection for the longfin smelt. The vote was 216 to 208 and only set how the debate would proceed.

2025-107.name: TICKET Act (Ticket Pricing Transparency)
2025-107.plain: The House passed the TICKET Act, 409 to 15. It would require ticket sellers to show the full price, including all fees, up front and bar selling tickets they do not actually hold. Sellers would also have to refund the total price if an event is canceled or postponed.

2025-108.name: Youth Poisoning Protection Act
2025-108.plain: The House voted to pass a bill that would ban consumer products with 10% or more sodium nitrite, with exceptions for certain drugs, medical devices, cosmetics, and food. It passed 378 to 42.

2025-109.name: Informing Consumers about Smart Devices Act
2025-109.plain: The House passed a bill, 415 to 9, requiring makers of internet-connected devices with a camera or microphone to tell buyers about that feature before they purchase. Phones and laptops are excluded.

2025-11.name: Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act
2025-11.plain: The House rejected a motion to send this bill back to committee, so it moved on toward a final vote. If passed, it would bar male-born athletes from women's and girls' sports programs at federally funded schools and colleges, treating that as a violation of Title IX.

2025-110.name: Glen Canyon Off-Road Vehicle Rule Repeal
2025-110.plain: The House voted 219 to 205 to pass a measure that would cancel a National Park Service rule limiting off-road vehicles in parts of the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area in Arizona and Utah. The rule had barred such vehicles on certain routes and limited their use on roads near Lake Powell.

2025-111.name: Revoking California Truck Emissions Waivers
2025-111.plain: The House voted 231 to 191 to pass a resolution that would cancel federal permission granted to California for its heavy-duty vehicle emission rules, including truck emission warranty and maintenance requirements.

2025-112.name: Revoking California Truck and Engine Pollution Waiver
2025-112.plain: The House voted 225 to 196 to pass a measure that would cancel the federal permission California had received for its stricter pollution standards on new heavy-duty trucks, large engines, and some off-road diesel equipment, starting with 2024 model years.

2025-113.name: Longfin Smelt Endangered Species Protection
2025-113.plain: The House voted 216 to 195 to pass a measure that cancels the federal listing of the San Francisco Bay-Delta longfin smelt as an endangered species, removing its protection under the Endangered Species Act.

2025-114.name: Revoking California's Vehicle Emissions Waiver
2025-114.plain: The House passed a joint resolution, 246 to 164, to revoke the federal waiver that let California enforce its Advanced Clean Cars II rules on low-emission and zero-emission vehicles. Revoking the waiver cancels the Environmental Protection Agency's decision to grant it.

2025-115.name: Study of Cancer Among Veterans Who Flew Aircraft
2025-115.plain: The House voted 376 to 5 to pass a bill requiring the Department of Veterans Affairs to arrange a study by the National Academies on how common cancer is among veterans who served as aircrew in fixed-wing aircraft, and how many die from it.

2025-116.name: Sanctions on Georgia-Linked Officials and Persons
2025-116.plain: The House voted to pass the MEGOBARI Act, 349 to 42. The bill requires the President to impose visa blocks on certain foreign persons, including some Georgian officials, who undermine Georgia's security or stability, and allows property blocks on them too.

2025-117.name: Procedural Vote on Gulf of America and Confucius Institute Bills
2025-117.plain: The House voted 206 to 200 to end debate and move toward a final vote on two bills. One would rename the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America, and the other would restrict Department of Homeland Security funding for colleges that have ties to Confucius Institutes. This vote was not on the bills themselves.

2025-118.name: Debate Rules for Gulf Renaming and Confucius Institute Bills
2025-118.plain: The House voted 213 to 209 to approve the rules for debating two measures: one to rename the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America, and one to restrict Department of Homeland Security funding for colleges that have ties to Confucius Institutes. The vote set debate rules and did not decide either measure itself.

2025-119.name: Stop Forced Organ Harvesting Act
2025-119.plain: The House passed a bill, 406 to 1, that would require sanctions on people and groups involved in forced organ harvesting and trafficking, and let the State Department deny or revoke passports of certain people convicted of related organ-transfer crimes.

2025-12.name: Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act
2025-12.plain: The House voted 218 to 206 to pass a bill that would bar male-born athletes from women's and girls' sports programs at federally funded schools and colleges, treating such participation as a violation of Title IX.

2025-120.name: Restricting Homeland Security Funds to Universities with China Ties
2025-120.plain: The House voted to pass a bill, 266 to 153, that would bar universities from receiving Homeland Security Department funds if they have relationships with certain Chinese-government-linked cultural institutes, talent programs, or Chinese military, police, or intelligence-linked schools, unless they end those relationships.

2025-121.name: Renaming the Gulf of Mexico
2025-121.plain: The House voted on whether to send the bill to committee, and the effort failed, 203 to 213. The bill would rename the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America and direct federal agencies to update their documents and maps.

2025-122.name: Renaming the Gulf of Mexico
2025-122.plain: The House passed a bill, 211 to 206, to rename the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America. It would direct federal agencies to update their documents and maps to use the new name.

2025-123.name: Support for Local Law Enforcement Officers
2025-123.plain: The House approved a resolution recognizing and thanking local police officers and their families, honoring those who have died in the line of duty, and encouraging cooperation between police and the communities they serve. The vote was 411 in favor and 1 against.

2025-124.name: Renaming Paterson Park Features for Bill Pascrell Jr
2025-124.plain: The House passed a bill renaming a trail bridge and a park at Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park in New Jersey after former Congressman Bill Pascrell Jr. The vote was 362 in favor and 50 against.

2025-125.name: Salem Maritime National Historical Park Redesignation Act
2025-125.plain: The House passed a bill renaming the Salem Maritime National Historic Site in Massachusetts as a national historical park. It also directs the Interior Department to study whether nearby sites tied to the area's maritime, coastal defense, and military history should be added to the park.

2025-126.name: Rule for Three Law Enforcement Bills
2025-126.plain: The House voted 216 to 204 to end debate and move to a final vote on a procedural step that sets the terms for considering three bills. The bills concern reports on violent attacks against law enforcement officers, changes to the Law Enforcement Officer Safety Act and concealed carry by officers, and letting federal officers buy their retired service weapons.

2025-127.name: Debate Rules for Three Law Enforcement Bills
2025-127.plain: The House voted 216 to 203 to approve the rules for debating three bills about law enforcement, covering reports on violent attacks against officers, officer safety and carrying concealed weapons, and officers buying retired service weapons. This was a procedural step that sets how long debate lasts and which amendments are allowed, not a final vote on the bills.

2025-128.name: LEOSA Reform Act
2025-128.plain: The House passed a bill, 229 to 193, that would let qualified active and retired law enforcement officers carry concealed firearms and ammunition in school zones, national parks, public places on state, local, or private property, and certain public federal facilities. It would also let states reduce how often retired officers must meet certain qualification standards.

2025-129.name: Resolution Calling for Action Against Antisemitism
2025-129.plain: The House approved a resolution calling on elected officials, faith leaders, and community leaders to speak out against antisemitism and teach the public about the contributions of Jewish Americans. The vote was 421 in favor and 1 against.

2025-13.name: POWER Act of 2025
2025-13.plain: The House passed the POWER Act, 419 to 2, using a fast-track process. The bill would let electric utilities that receive emergency help to restore power also carry out cost-effective hazard mitigation work at the same time, and allow them to receive certain disaster hazard mitigation assistance for the same facility.

2025-130.name: Federal Law Enforcement Officer Service Weapon Purchase Act
2025-130.plain: The House passed this bill 234 to 182. It would direct the General Services Administration to set up a program letting federal law enforcement officers buy a retired firearm from the agency that issued it to them.

2025-131.name: Law Enforcement Officer Safety and Wellness Data Bill
2025-131.plain: The House passed a bill, 403 to 11, requiring the Department of Justice to report on targeted attacks on police officers, whether such attacks could be added to existing crime reporting systems, and what mental health resources are available to officers.

2025-132.name: Strengthening the Quad Act
2025-132.plain: The House voted 334 to 51 to pass a bill directing the State Department to seek a working group with Japan, Australia, and India on closer cooperation, and to report to Congress on a strategy for engagement with the Quad, a coalition of those countries and the United States.

2025-133.name: Simplifying Forms for Veterans Claims
2025-133.plain: The House passed a bill, 386 to 1, requiring the Department of Veterans Affairs to get an outside research center to review its claim forms and recommend ways to make them clearer and better organized. The VA must put certain recommendations into effect within two years.

2025-134.name: Rule Governing Debate on Two Agency Rule Disapprovals
2025-134.plain: The House voted 215 to 207 to end debate and move to a final vote on a procedural rule for considering two resolutions that would nullify agency rules: one on bank merger reviews and one on Clean Air Act reclassification of major sources, along with a budget-related waiver.

2025-135.name: Debate Rules for Two Resolutions on Agency Rules
2025-135.plain: The House voted 210 to 208 to approve the rules for debating two measures that would overturn federal agency rules, one on bank mergers and one on air pollution from major sources. This was a procedural step, not a vote on those measures themselves.

2025-136.name: ANCHOR Act: Research Ship Cybersecurity and Communications
2025-136.plain: The House passed the ANCHOR Act 412 to 11. The bill requires the National Science Foundation to create a plan to improve cybersecurity and communications on U.S. academic research ships, including how much it would cost and how long upgrades would take.

2025-137.name: Bank Merger Review Rule Repeal
2025-137.plain: The House passed a measure to cancel a rule that changed how federal regulators review proposed bank mergers, including removing automatic approvals and streamlined application forms. The vote was 220 to 207.

2025-139.name: Procedural Vote on Reconciliation Bill (H.R. 1)
2025-139.plain: The House voted 217 to 211 to take up a measure that would set the rules for debating the reconciliation bill H.R. 1. Republicans voted yes and Democrats voted no.

2025-14.name: Tennessee Valley Authority Salary Transparency Act
2025-14.plain: The House voted 423 to 0 to pass a bill requiring the Tennessee Valley Authority, a government electricity and river-management corporation, to again file an annual financial report with Congress each March. It would also limit the public salary details in that report to employees paid above the GS-13 basic pay rate.

2025-140.name: Procedural Vote on Reconciliation Bill
2025-140.plain: The House voted 216 to 211 to begin considering H.R. 1, a reconciliation measure, with Republicans in favor and Democrats opposed. The vote decided whether to take up the bill, not its final passage.

2025-141.name: Procedural Vote on Budget Reconciliation Bill
2025-141.plain: The House voted 213 to 211 to end debate on a rule for H.R. 1, moving toward a final vote on the bill itself. This was a procedural step, not the vote on the measure.

2025-142.name: Debate Rules for the Reconciliation Bill (H.R. 1)
2025-142.plain: The House voted 217 to 212 to approve the rules for debating H.R. 1, a reconciliation bill, which sets how long debate lasts and which changes may be offered. This was a procedural step, not a final vote on the bill itself.

2025-143.name: EPA Clean Air Act Emissions Rule Disapproval
2025-143.plain: The House voted 216 to 212 to pass a resolution that would cancel an Environmental Protection Agency rule. The rule required facilities that reclassify as area sources of hazardous air pollution to keep emission controls that apply to major sources.

2025-144.name: Reconciliation Bill Recommittal Vote
2025-144.plain: The House voted on whether to send the reconciliation bill, which changes SNAP food assistance and other federal programs, back to committee. The motion failed 212 to 216, so the bill moved on toward a final vote.

2025-145.name: Budget Reconciliation Bill on Taxes, Spending, and Debt Limit
2025-145.plain: The House voted 215 to 214 to pass a large bill that cuts taxes, changes spending on many federal programs, including changes to food assistance work rules, and raises the federal debt limit.

2025-146.name: Connecting Small Businesses with Career and Technical Education Graduates Act
2025-146.plain: The House voted to pass a bill requiring Small Business Development Centers and Women's Business Centers to give small businesses information about hiring graduates of career and technical education programs, and to connect them with those programs where appropriate. The bill passed 396 to 5.

2025-147.name: 7(a) Loan Agent Oversight Act
2025-147.plain: The House voted 405 to 3 to pass a bill requiring the Small Business Administration to publish an annual report on fee-based agents who help businesses apply for 7(a) loans, including fraud cases and referral fees paid.

2025-148.name: Procedural Vote on Four Small Business and Opioid Bills
2025-148.plain: The House voted 213 to 206 to end debate and move to a final vote on a package of four bills, including one on opioid treatment and others on Small Business Administration offices, loans, and lending companies. This was a procedural vote, not a vote on the bills themselves.

2025-149.name: Debate Rules for Four Small Business and Opioid Bills
2025-149.plain: The House voted 217 to 208 to approve the rules for debating four bills, covering opioid treatment programs and Small Business Administration loans and offices. The vote set how long debate would last and which amendments were allowed; it did not vote on the bills themselves.

2025-15.name: Tax Rules for Certain Taiwan Residents
2025-15.plain: The House voted 423 to 1 to pass a bill that sets special federal income tax rules for certain residents of Taiwan who earn income from U.S. sources.

2025-150.name: Amendment to the SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Reauthorization Act
2025-150.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Reauthorization Act, which renews federal programs on substance use, overdoses, and mental health. The amendment failed on a tie vote, 213 to 213.

2025-151.name: SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Reauthorization Act
2025-151.plain: The House passed this bill 366 to 57. It renews and revises federal programs on substance use disorders, overdoses, and mental health, including prevention, treatment, and crisis-line cybersecurity efforts.

2025-152.name: Save SBA from Sanctuary Cities Act
2025-152.plain: The House voted 202 to 210 against sending the Save SBA from Sanctuary Cities Act back to committee, so the bill moved on to a final vote. The bill would require the Small Business Administration to move any office it finds is in a sanctuary jurisdiction to another location within 60 days.

2025-153.name: Moving Small Business Administration Offices Out of Sanctuary Cities
2025-153.plain: The House voted 211 to 199 to pass a bill requiring the Small Business Administration to move any local, district, or regional office located in a sanctuary jurisdiction to a place that is not one, within 60 days of a public finding. It would also bar the agency from opening new offices in such jurisdictions.

2025-154.name: Limit on Small Business Lending Companies
2025-154.plain: The House voted on whether to send the CEASE Act back to committee, which would have delayed the bill. The motion failed, 201 to 212, so the House moved on to a final vote on the bill. The bill would cap at 16 the number of for-profit small business lending companies allowed to make 7(a) loans at any time.

2025-155.name: CEASE Act of 2025
2025-155.plain: The House passed the CEASE Act, 214 to 198. The bill would limit the number of for-profit small business lending companies allowed to make 7(a) loans to no more than 16 at any time.

2025-156.name: American Entrepreneurs First Act
2025-156.plain: The House voted to pass a bill changing Small Business Administration 7(a) and 504 loan applications so they require the applicant's date of birth and a certification of U.S. citizenship, nationality, or lawful permanent residency, and making certain immigration statuses ineligible for these loans. The bill passed 217 to 190.

2025-157.name: American Cargo for American Ships Act
2025-157.plain: The House passed a bill requiring that equipment, materials, and goods paid for by the Department of Transportation and shipped by sea travel on U.S.-flagged commercial vessels, to the extent such ships are available at fair and reasonable rates. The vote was 373 in favor and 14 against.

2025-158.name: Denouncing the Boulder, Colorado Antisemitic Attack
2025-158.plain: The House voted to approve a resolution condemning the antisemitic terrorist attack in Boulder, Colorado, and it passed 280 to 113. Republicans voted 205 in favor and none against; Democrats voted 75 in favor and 113 against.

2025-159.name: Condemning Rising Attacks on Jewish Americans
2025-159.plain: The House voted 400 to 0 to approve a resolution condemning ideologically motivated attacks on Jewish people in the United States, including the June 2025 attack in Boulder, Colorado, and reaffirming the House's commitment to fighting antisemitism and politically motivated violence.

2025-16.name: Preventing Violence Against Women by Illegal Aliens Act
2025-16.plain: The House voted 206 to 213 on a motion to send this bill back to committee, and the motion failed, so the bill moved toward a final vote. The bill would make certain sex offenses and domestic violence-related acts grounds for denying entry to or deporting non-U.S. nationals.

2025-160.name: Rule for Four Bills on D.C. Voting, Immigration, Police, and Fentanyl
2025-160.plain: The House voted 213 to 206 to end debate and move to a final vote on a procedural package covering four bills: one on voting in D.C. elections by non-citizens, one on D.C. complying with federal immigration laws, one on D.C. police discipline, and one on fentanyl-related drug scheduling. The vote was not on the bills themselves.

2025-161.name: House Debate Rules for Four D.C. and Drug Measures
2025-161.plain: The House voted 211 to 206 to approve rules for debating four measures, covering voting in D.C. elections, immigration law in D.C., police discipline in D.C., and fentanyl-related drugs. The vote set how long debate would last and which changes could be offered; it did not itself decide any of those measures.

2025-162.name: Protecting Our Nation's Capital Emergency Act
2025-162.plain: The House voted 235 to 178 to pass a bill that would undo 2023 changes to D.C. rules on disciplining Metropolitan Police officers. It would reinstate a 90-day time limit for starting discipline, let discipline be negotiated in union contracts, remove the police chief's power to raise a trial board's recommended penalty, and drop a requirement to post online schedules of termination hearings.

2025-163.name: Barring Noncitizen Voting in D.C. Local Elections
2025-163.plain: The House passed a bill that would stop noncitizens from voting in District of Columbia elections and would repeal a 2022 D.C. law that allowed some noncitizen residents to vote in local elections. The vote was 266 in favor and 148 against.

2025-164.name: Rule Vote on Rescinding Budget Authority
2025-164.plain: The House voted 210 to 204 to end debate and move to a final vote on a bill that would cancel certain funding the President proposed rescinding in June 2025. This was a procedural vote, not a vote on the bill itself.

2025-165.name: Debate Rules for Rescissions Bill
2025-165.plain: The House voted 213 to 207 to approve the rules for debating a bill that would cancel certain previously approved federal spending, first proposed by the President in June 2025. This vote set debate rules only and did not decide the bill itself.

2025-166.name: HALT Fentanyl Act
2025-166.plain: The House passed the HALT Fentanyl Act by 321 to 104. The bill would place fentanyl-related substances as a class under the strictest federal drug category and apply the same penalties and quantity thresholds used for fentanyl analogues, and it changes some registration rules for drug research.

2025-167.name: Rescissions Act of 2025 Recommittal Vote
2025-167.plain: The House voted on whether to send the Rescissions Act of 2025 back to committee, and the motion failed 208 to 218. The bill would cancel specified unspent funds for the State Department, USAID, several independent agencies, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

2025-168.name: Rescissions Act of 2025
2025-168.plain: The House passed a bill, 214 to 212, to cancel certain unspent funds previously provided to the State Department, the U.S. Agency for International Development, several independent agencies, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

2025-17.name: Preventing Violence Against Women by Illegal Aliens Act
2025-17.plain: The House voted 274 to 145 to pass a bill that would make certain non-U.S. nationals inadmissible or deportable for convictions or admitted acts such as stalking, child abuse, sex offenses, and domestic violence, and would widen the domestic violence crimes that make them deportable.

2025-170.name: District of Columbia Federal Immigration Compliance Act
2025-170.plain: The House voted on whether to send a bill about cooperation between Washington, D.C. and federal immigration enforcement back to committee, and the motion failed 205 to 215. The bill would bar D.C. from limiting information sharing on immigration status and from declining certain federal requests to hold people in custody, with exceptions for crime victims and witnesses.

2025-171.name: District of Columbia Immigration Cooperation Bill
2025-171.plain: The House passed a bill barring D.C. from limiting its cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, such as sharing immigration status information or honoring federal detainer requests, with exceptions for crime victims and witnesses. The vote was 224 in favor and 194 against.

2025-172.name: Sanction Sea Pirates Act
2025-172.plain: The House passed a bill, 392 to 14, that would require the President to impose visa and property sanctions on foreign individuals or groups found to knowingly engage in piracy. It also sets civil and criminal penalties for violating those sanctions.

2025-173.name: Fair Investment Opportunities for Professional Experts Act
2025-173.plain: The House voted 397 to 12 to pass a bill that would let people qualify to invest in certain private offerings based on professional knowledge gained through education or work experience, not only on income or net worth. The bill also writes into law some existing rules for who qualifies as an accredited investor.

2025-174.name: Helping Small Businesses Raise Money
2025-174.plain: The House passed a bill, 321 to 87, that would require the Securities and Exchange Commission's small business office to share educational resources on raising money for underrepresented, rural, and disaster-affected small businesses, and to meet yearly with state securities regulators.

2025-175.name: Motion to Table Impeachment of President Trump
2025-175.plain: The House voted 344 to 79 to set aside a resolution to impeach President Donald Trump over an alleged abuse of presidential power by overstepping Congress's power to declare war. Setting it aside ends the resolution.

2025-176.name: Procedural Vote on Several Immigration and Military Spending Bills
2025-176.plain: The House voted 219 to 208 to end debate and move to a final vote on a package of measures covering military construction and veterans spending, border reporting, drunk-driving deportation, and a resolution condemning the June 2025 Los Angeles riots. This vote did not decide the measures themselves.

2025-177.name: Debate Rules for Four Measures
2025-177.plain: The House voted 217 to 206 to approve the rules for debating four measures, including a military construction and veterans funding bill, a border reporting bill, a bill on driving while intoxicated and deportation, and a resolution condemning the June 2025 Los Angeles riots. This vote set debate time and allowed amendments but did not itself decide those measures.

2025-179.name: Condemning Attacks on Minnesota Lawmakers
2025-179.plain: The House voted 424 to 0 to approve a resolution condemning the June 14, 2025 attacks on Minnesota state legislators. It calls for unity and rejecting political violence, and honors those killed and injured and the officers who responded.

2025-18.name: Hershel Woody Williams National Medal of Honor Monument Location Act
2025-18.plain: The House voted 414 to 0 to pass a bill requiring the national monument honoring Medal of Honor recipients to be placed within the Reserve, the central axis of the National Mall running from the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial and from the White House to the Jefferson Memorial.

2025-180.name: Spending Bill for Military Construction, Veterans, Agriculture, and Congress
2025-180.plain: The House voted 219 to 206 to add an amendment to this spending bill, which would provide funding for military construction and housing, veterans programs, agriculture and food safety agencies, and the Senate and other congressional support agencies.

2025-181.name: Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, Agriculture, and Legislative Branch Funding Bill
2025-181.plain: The House voted 216 to 208 against sending this bill back to committee, so it moved on toward a final vote. The bill would fund military construction and housing, veterans programs, agriculture and food safety agencies, and the Senate and related congressional agencies for 2026.

2025-182.name: Military Construction, Veterans, Agriculture, and Legislative Branch Funding
2025-182.plain: The House voted 218 to 206 to pass a bill that provides federal funding for military construction and housing, veterans affairs, agriculture and the Food and Drug Administration, and the Senate and related congressional agencies.

2025-183.name: Deporting Non-Citizens Convicted of Drunk Driving
2025-183.plain: The House passed a bill, 246 to 160, that would make drunk or impaired driving grounds to bar a non-citizen from entering the United States or to deport them, if they were convicted of the offense, or for admission, had admitted to the acts behind it.

2025-184.name: Special Interest Alien Reporting Act
2025-184.plain: The House passed this bill 231 to 182. It would require the Department of Homeland Security to report each month on how many people who may pose a national security risk tried to enter the United States unlawfully, their nationalities or last countries of residence, and where they were encountered.

2025-185.name: Condemning the June 2025 Los Angeles Riots
2025-185.plain: The House voted 215 to 195 to approve a resolution condemning the violent June 2025 riots in Los Angeles, California. The resolution also expresses gratitude to law enforcement agencies, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, for their work during the demonstrations.

2025-186.name: Procedural Vote on Senate Amendment to Reconciliation Bill
2025-186.plain: The House voted 212 to 211 to take up a Senate change to a bill about budget reconciliation. Republicans voted yes and Democrats voted no. The vote only decided whether the House would consider the change; it did not itself enact the measure.

2025-187.name: Procedural Vote on Senate Amendment to Reconciliation Bill
2025-187.plain: The House voted 214 to 212 to end debate and move to a final vote on the Senate's changes to a budget reconciliation bill. This was a procedural step, not a vote on the bill itself.

2025-188.name: Budget Reconciliation Bill Amendment
2025-188.plain: The House voted 220 to 212 to approve a change to a bill that the Senate had altered. Republicans voted yes and Democrats voted no. The change would add a version of the Senate's amendment to the bill, with the vote following party lines.

2025-189.name: House Debate Rules for Senate Amendment to H.R. 1
2025-189.plain: The House voted 219 to 213 to approve the rules for debating changes the Senate made to H.R. 1, a bill about reconciliation. This was a procedural step that sets how long debate lasts and which amendments are allowed, not a final vote on the bill itself.

2025-19.name: MAPWaters Act of 2025 (Public Waterway Access Data)
2025-19.plain: The House passed the MAPWaters Act by 413 votes to 0 under a fast-track process requiring two-thirds support. The bill directs the Forest Service and Interior Department to publish online maps and data on public access to federal waterways for recreation and on federal fishing restrictions.

2025-190.name: Budget Reconciliation Bill With Tax, Spending and Debt Limit Changes
2025-190.plain: The House voted 218 to 214 to accept the Senate's changes to this bill. The bill would reduce taxes, change spending on various federal programs, and raise the federal debt limit. Changes include tightening work requirements for some food assistance recipients.

2025-191.name: Understanding Cybersecurity of Mobile Networks Act
2025-191.plain: The House voted 360 to 10 to pass a bill requiring the National Telecommunications and Information Administration to examine and report on the cybersecurity of mobile networks and how vulnerable they and mobile devices are to cyberattacks and surveillance.

2025-192.name: Consumer Safety Technology Act
2025-192.plain: The House passed the Consumer Safety Technology Act, 336 to 36. The bill would set up a pilot program for the Consumer Product Safety Commission to test artificial intelligence for tracking product injuries and hazards, and require reports on blockchain technology and digital tokens.

2025-193.name: Jocelyn Nungaray National Wildlife Refuge Act
2025-193.plain: The House voted 372 to 0 to pass a bill renaming the Anahuac National Wildlife Refuge in Texas as the Jocelyn Nungaray National Wildlife Refuge. The bill also gives legal authority to an earlier executive order that made the same name change.

2025-194.name: Procedural Vote on Defense Spending and Digital Assets Bills
2025-194.plain: The House voted 211 to 210 to end debate and move toward a final vote on several bills, including Defense Department spending and rules for digital currencies and stablecoins. This was a procedural step, not a vote on the bills themselves.

2025-195.name: Debate Rules for Defense Spending and Crypto Bills
2025-195.plain: The House voted on the rules for debating several bills, including defense funding and cryptocurrency regulation. The vote failed, 196 in favor to 223 against, so those debate rules were not approved.

2025-196.name: Communications Security Act
2025-196.plain: The House passed the Communications Security Act, 380 to 33. The bill would give legal authority to an FCC advisory council on the security and reliability of communications networks, and exempt it from the usual two-year expiration rule.

2025-197.name: Rule Setting Debate on Defense Funding, Crypto and Stablecoins
2025-197.plain: The House voted 215 to 211 on a procedural motion to reconsider a rule that sets the terms for debate on several bills. The bills cover defense funding for fiscal year 2026, regulation of digital commodities, limits on Federal Reserve services and central bank digital currency, and payment stablecoins.

2025-198.name: Debate Rules for Defense Spending and Digital Asset Bills
2025-198.plain: The House voted 217 to 212 to approve the rules for debating several measures, including a defense spending bill and bills on digital assets and stablecoins. This was a procedural step that sets how long debate lasts and which changes are allowed, not a vote on those measures themselves.

2025-199.name: Digital Asset Market Clarity Act
2025-199.plain: The House voted 294 to 134 to pass the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. It would set up federal rules for digital commodities, which are digital assets whose value depends on a blockchain, with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission generally overseeing their trading.

2025-20.name: Procedural Vote on Forest Management and Immigration Bills
2025-20.plain: The House voted 214 to 204 to end debate and move toward final votes on a rule covering two bills: one to speed up forest management work on federal, BLM and Tribal lands, and one to require Homeland Security to take into custody people charged with theft. This vote was not on the bills themselves.

2025-200.name: GENIUS Act (Stablecoin Regulation)
2025-200.plain: The House passed the GENIUS Act, 308 to 122. The bill sets rules for payment stablecoins, which are digital currencies that issuers must redeem for a fixed value, requiring them to be backed one-to-one by reserves such as U.S. currency and Treasury securities.

2025-201.name: Ban on a Federal Digital Dollar
2025-201.plain: The House passed a bill, 219 to 210, that would bar the Federal Reserve from offering accounts or services directly to individuals or issuing a central bank digital currency, a digital dollar. It would also limit the Fed's Board from using or studying such a currency for monetary policy, with some exceptions.

2025-202.name: Rescissions Act of 2025 Procedural Vote
2025-202.plain: The House voted 218 to 211 to end debate and move to a final vote on a measure that would cancel previously approved federal funding, as requested by the President in June 2025. Republicans voted yes and Democrats voted no. This was a procedural vote, not the final vote on the measure itself.

2025-203.name: Rescissions Act of 2025 Final Approval
2025-203.plain: The House voted 216 to 213 to approve a resolution that sends the Rescissions Act of 2025, as amended by the Senate, to final passage. The act would cancel certain previously approved federal funds that the President asked Congress to rescind in June 2025.

2025-204.name: Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026
2025-204.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides funding for military activities. The amendment was rejected, 365 votes against to 63 in favor.

2025-205.name: Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026
2025-205.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides funding for military activities such as personnel, operations, equipment, and research. The amendment was rejected, with 6 in favor and 421 opposed.

2025-206.name: Amendment to the Defense Appropriations Act
2025-206.plain: The House rejected a proposal to change the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides funding for military activities. The vote was 104 in favor and 326 against, so the change was not added.

2025-207.name: Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026 Amendment
2025-207.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides money for military activities. The amendment was rejected, with 6 voting yes and 422 voting no.

2025-208.name: Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026 Amendment
2025-208.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides funding for military activities. The amendment was rejected, 30 in favor and 400 against.

2025-209.name: Department of Defense Spending Bill Amendment
2025-209.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides funding for military activities. The amendment was rejected, 76 in favor and 353 against.

2025-21.name: Debate Rules for Forest Management and Immigration Bills
2025-21.plain: The House voted 213 to 204 to approve the rules for debating two measures: one to speed up forest management work on federal and tribal lands, and one to require immigration custody for people charged with theft. This vote set the debate rules only and did not decide either measure itself.

2025-210.name: Defense Spending Bill Amendment
2025-210.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides funding for military activities. The amendment was rejected, 76 in favor and 355 against.

2025-211.name: Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026
2025-211.plain: The House voted against sending the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026 back to committee, so the bill moved on to a final vote. The bill provides funding to the Department of Defense for military activities in fiscal year 2026.

2025-212.name: Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026
2025-212.plain: The House passed a bill providing funding for Department of Defense military activities for fiscal year 2026, by a vote of 221 to 209. The bill covers military personnel, operations, weapons purchases, research, and health programs, among other areas.

2025-213.name: ZIP Codes for 74 Communities
2025-213.plain: The House passed a bill, 278 to 121, requiring the Postal Service to give each of 74 named communities its own single, unique ZIP Code.

2025-214.name: Improving Access to Small Business Information Act
2025-214.plain: The House voted 387 to 12 to pass a bill that exempts the SEC's Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation from certain federal rules on collecting information from the public, with some exceptions, such as telling people why their information is being collected.

2025-215.name: Wabeno Economic Development Act
2025-215.plain: The House passed a bill, 410 to 1, that would require the Forest Service to sell about 14 acres of federal land in Wisconsin, including mineral rights, to a local company at market value. It also directs the Interior Department to review federal permitting for stone, sand, and gravel development on federal lands.

2025-216.name: Great Lakes Mass Marking Program Act
2025-216.plain: The House passed a bill, 360 to 57, to give the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service legal authority for its program of tagging large numbers of hatchery-raised fish in the Great Lakes. The bill lets the agency buy supplies and hire staff, and requires it to share the tagging data with federal, state, and tribal fish managers.

2025-217.name: Enhancing Multi-Class Share Disclosures Act
2025-217.plain: The House passed a bill requiring companies with multiple classes of shares that have different voting rights to disclose information about directors, executives, and major shareholders in proxy materials. The vote was 381 in favor and 31 against.

2025-218.name: Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025
2025-218.plain: The House voted to pass the Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, 399 to 12. The vote used a fast-track process, which skips amendments and requires two-thirds support.

2025-219.name: Made-in-America Defense Act
2025-219.plain: The House passed the Made-in-America Defense Act, 395 to 20. The bill would require the State Department to review each year which military equipment and services now sold only through government-to-government deals could also be sold directly by U.S. companies to foreign governments, and to report its findings to Congress.

2025-22.name: Wounded Knee Massacre Memorial and Sacred Site Act
2025-22.plain: The House passed a bill, 416 to 0, that would place about 40 acres in Oglala Lakota County, South Dakota, into restricted status for the Oglala Sioux Tribe and Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe. The land would be kept as a memorial and sacred site, with commercial development and gaming banned.

2025-220.name: Stop Chinese Fentanyl Act
2025-220.plain: The House voted 407 to 4 to pass the Stop Chinese Fentanyl Act. It would let the government sanction certain Chinese companies and officials involved in opioid trafficking, and extend a yearly report to Congress on foreign opioid traffickers through 2029.

2025-221.name: Energy and Water Spending Bill and Land Management Rules
2025-221.plain: The House voted 212 to 209 to end debate and move toward a final vote on a rule for considering a 2026 energy and water spending bill and three resolutions to overturn Bureau of Land Management land-use plans. This was a procedural step, not a vote on the measures themselves.

2025-222.name: Debate Rules for Energy-Water Spending and Land Measures
2025-222.plain: The House voted 212 to 208 to approve the rules for debating a bill providing funding for energy and water programs for fiscal year 2026, along with three measures to overturn Bureau of Land Management land-use plans. The vote set debate time and allowed amendments; it did not vote on those measures themselves.

2025-223.name: Censure of Representative LaMonica McIver
2025-223.plain: The House voted 215 to 207 to set aside a resolution that would have censured Representative LaMonica McIver and removed her from the Homeland Security Committee. The resolution is therefore not moving forward.

2025-224.name: Opening Eastern Montana Federal Land to Coal Leasing
2025-224.plain: The House voted 211 to 208 to pass a measure that would cancel a federal land-management decision for the Miles City area in eastern Montana, which had made no acres available for coal leasing. The change would open this land to coal leasing.

2025-225.name: Central Yukon Land Management Plan Rollback
2025-225.plain: The House passed a measure, 215 to 210, to cancel a Bureau of Land Management plan for about 3.6 million acres of Alaska's Central Yukon area, including 21 areas of critical environmental concern or research natural areas.

2025-226.name: Overturning North Dakota Federal Land Management Plan
2025-226.plain: The House passed a resolution, 215 to 211, to cancel a Bureau of Land Management plan for federal land in North Dakota. The plan had limited oil and gas development in low-potential areas and restricted new coal leasing to areas within four miles of existing mines.

2025-227.name: Energy and Water Development Appropriations Act, 2026 Amendment
2025-227.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides funding for Army Corps of Engineers civil works projects, Bureau of Reclamation programs, Department of Energy programs, and several independent agencies. The amendment failed, 195 in favor to 235 against.

2025-228.name: Energy and Water Development Spending Bill, 2026
2025-228.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides money for Army Corps of Engineers water projects, Interior Department water programs, Energy Department programs, and several independent agencies. The amendment was rejected, 143 in favor to 285 against.

2025-229.name: Energy and Water Development Spending Bill Amendment
2025-229.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides funding for Army Corps of Engineers civil works, Bureau of Reclamation, and Department of Energy programs. The amendment was rejected, 77 in favor to 347 opposed.

2025-23.name: Laken Riley Act
2025-23.plain: The House voted to pass the Laken Riley Act, 263 to 156. It would require detaining certain non-citizens arrested for specified crimes such as theft, assault of a law enforcement officer, or crimes causing death or serious injury, and would let states sue the federal government over certain immigration enforcement decisions.

2025-230.name: Energy and Water Development Appropriations Act, 2026 Amendment
2025-230.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides funding for Army Corps of Engineers water projects and Department of Energy programs. The amendment was rejected, 286 to 140.

2025-231.name: Energy and Water Spending Bill Amendment
2025-231.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides funding for Army Corps of Engineers civil works, the Bureau of Reclamation, the Department of Energy, and several independent agencies. The amendment was rejected, 120 in favor to 306 against.

2025-232.name: Energy and Water Development Spending Bill Amendment
2025-232.plain: The House rejected an amendment to the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides funding for Army Corps of Engineers water projects, Bureau of Reclamation programs, Department of Energy programs, and several independent agencies. The vote was 124 in favor and 303 against.

2025-233.name: Energy and Water Development Spending Bill Amendment
2025-233.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides funding for Army Corps of Engineers projects, Bureau of Reclamation, and Department of Energy programs. The amendment was rejected, 127 in favor to 299 against.

2025-234.name: Energy and Water Spending Bill Amendment
2025-234.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the Energy and Water Development spending bill for 2026, which funds Army Corps of Engineers water projects, Interior Department water programs, and Energy Department programs. The amendment was rejected, 120 in favor and 307 against.

2025-235.name: Energy and Water Development Spending Bill Amendment
2025-235.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026, which funds Army Corps of Engineers projects, Bureau of Reclamation work, and Department of Energy programs. The amendment failed, with 120 in favor and 302 against.

2025-236.name: Energy and Water Development Spending Bill Amendment
2025-236.plain: The House rejected an amendment to the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026, which provides funding for Army Corps of Engineers civil works projects, Bureau of Reclamation programs, Department of Energy programs, and several independent agencies. The vote was 127 in favor and 297 against.

2025-237.name: Energy and Water Spending Bill, 2026 Amendment
2025-237.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the Energy and Water Development spending bill for 2026, which funds Army Corps of Engineers water projects, Interior Department water programs, and Energy Department programs. The amendment was rejected, 76 in favor and 351 against.

2025-238.name: Energy and Water Spending Bill Sent-Back Motion
2025-238.plain: The House voted on whether to send the Energy and Water Development spending bill back to committee. The motion failed, 209 to 218, so the bill moved on toward a final vote. The bill would provide funding for Army Corps of Engineers projects, Energy Department programs, and several independent agencies in 2026.

2025-239.name: Energy and Water Development Spending Bill
2025-239.plain: The House passed a bill providing funding for Army Corps of Engineers water projects, Bureau of Reclamation programs, Department of Energy programs, and several independent agencies, by a vote of 214 to 213.

2025-24.name: Rapid Ohia Death Response Act
2025-24.plain: The House passed a bill to research and control Rapid Ohia Death, a fungal disease that kills ohia trees in Hawaii, by coordinating federal agencies, the state, and landowners. The vote was 359 in favor and 62 against.

2025-240.name: SPACE Act of 2025
2025-240.plain: The House passed the SPACE Act by 397 to 1. The bill directs the General Services Administration to work with federal agencies on sharing office space in federally leased buildings, including setting measurable goals and reporting to Congress within six months.

2025-241.name: Federal Building Security Personnel Oversight Act
2025-241.plain: The House voted 402 to 0 to pass a bill requiring the Federal Protective Service to test and improve the security guards it hires to protect federal buildings, and to report to Congress on those efforts. It also requires a review of the system used to track guard availability and a plan to notify building tenants about gaps in coverage.

2025-242.name: Rules for Defense Authorization and Immigration Penalties Bills
2025-242.plain: The House voted 213 to 207 to pass a procedural step that sets the rules for debating two bills: one on defense programs and military personnel levels, and one to increase penalties for people who illegally re-enter the U.S. after being removed. The vote was to end debate and move to a final vote, not on the bills themselves.

2025-243.name: Debate Rules for Defense and Immigration Bills
2025-243.plain: The House voted 210 to 207 to approve the rules for debating two other measures: one that authorizes funding for military activities and defense programs for 2026, and one that would increase penalties for people who illegally enter or re-enter the U.S. after being removed. This vote set the debate rules only and was not a vote on those measures themselves.

2025-244.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Act
2025-244.plain: The House voted 261 to 167 to add an amendment to the annual defense bill that sets policy and spending authority for military programs for fiscal year 2026. The bill also covers military construction and certain Energy Department national security programs.

2025-245.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Bill
2025-245.plain: The House voted 221 to 210 to add an amendment to the annual defense bill, which sets policy and authorizes spending for military programs for fiscal year 2026. Most Republicans voted yes and most Democrats voted no.

2025-246.name: Amendment to the 2026 Defense Authorization Bill
2025-246.plain: The House voted 221 to 207 to add an amendment to the Streamlining Procurement for Effective Execution and Delivery and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, which sets policies for Defense Department programs, military construction, and related national security activities.

2025-247.name: Amendment to Defense Authorization Act for 2026
2025-247.plain: The House voted 227 to 201 to add an amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026. That bill sets policies and authorizes programs for military, defense and national security activities.

2025-248.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Bill for 2026
2025-248.plain: The House voted 221 to 210 to add an amendment to the Streamlining Procurement for Effective Execution and Delivery and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, a bill that sets policies for military programs and defense activities for 2026.

2025-249.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Act
2025-249.plain: The House voted 219 to 209 to add an amendment to the annual defense policy bill that sets rules for military programs for fiscal year 2026. The amendment was adopted.

2025-25.name: Fix Our Forests Act
2025-25.plain: The House passed the Fix Our Forests Act, 279 to 141. The bill sets rules for managing federal forests to reduce wildfire risk, speeds up reviews of certain forest projects, and limits some legal challenges to them.

2025-250.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Bill
2025-250.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the annual defense bill, which sets policy and authorizes programs for the military and related national security activities. The amendment was rejected, 209 in favor and 224 against.

2025-251.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Act
2025-251.plain: The House voted 224 to 208 to add an amendment to the annual defense policy bill, which sets policy for military programs, equipment, and personnel for fiscal year 2026. Most Republicans supported the change and most Democrats opposed it.

2025-252.name: Amendment to the 2026 Defense Authorization Bill
2025-252.plain: The House voted 228 to 205 to add an amendment to the annual defense bill that sets policy and authorizes funding for military programs for fiscal year 2026. Most Republicans voted yes and most Democrats voted no.

2025-253.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Act
2025-253.plain: The House voted 222 to 210 to add an amendment to the annual defense policy bill, which sets rules and policies for military programs for fiscal year 2026. The amendment was approved, with most Republicans voting yes and most Democrats voting no.

2025-254.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Act
2025-254.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the Streamlining Procurement for Effective Execution and Delivery and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, which sets defense policies and authorities for 2026. The amendment was rejected, 194 in favor to 236 opposed.

2025-255.name: Amendment to the 2026 Defense Authorization Bill
2025-255.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the 2026 defense bill, which sets policies and authorizes programs for the Department of Defense, military construction, and related national security activities. The amendment was rejected, 60 in favor to 372 against.

2025-256.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Act
2025-256.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the annual defense policy bill, which sets policies for military programs for fiscal year 2026. The amendment was rejected, 60 in favor to 370 against.

2025-257.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Bill
2025-257.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the 2026 defense policy bill, which sets rules and authorizes programs for the military and related national security work. The amendment was rejected, with 9 in favor and 422 against.

2025-258.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Bill
2025-258.plain: The House voted 219 to 211 to add an amendment to the annual defense policy bill, which sets rules and authorizes activities for military programs for 2026. Most Republicans supported the change and most Democrats opposed it.

2025-259.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Act
2025-259.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the annual defense bill that sets Pentagon policies, programs, and military spending authority for 2026. The amendment failed, with 200 votes in favor and 228 against.

2025-26.name: Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act
2025-26.plain: The House voted on whether to send this bill back to committee, and the motion failed 205 to 216, so the bill moved on toward a final vote. The bill would require care for any child born alive after an abortion or attempted abortion, require immediate hospital admission, and set fines or up to five years in prison for violations.

2025-260.name: Amendment to Defense Authorization Bill
2025-260.plain: The House voted 430 to 3 to add an amendment to the annual defense policy bill for 2026, which sets rules and authorizes military programs. Most members of both parties supported the change.

2025-261.name: Defense Authorization Bill: Motion to Send Back to Committee
2025-261.plain: The House voted on whether to send the annual defense policy bill back to committee for changes before a final vote. The motion failed, 208 for and 219 against, so the House moved on toward the final vote on the bill, which sets policy and authorizes military programs and activities for 2026.

2025-262.name: Annual Defense Policy Bill for 2026
2025-262.plain: The House voted 231 to 196 to pass a bill setting policies for military programs, equipment, and operations for fiscal year 2026. It also covers military construction, some national security programs, and changes to how the military buys equipment.

2025-263.name: Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, Agriculture, and Legislative Branch Funding
2025-263.plain: The House voted on a motion to give instructions to negotiators working out differences on a funding bill for military construction, veterans programs, agriculture, and Congress. The motion failed, 211 in favor to 213 against.

2025-264.name: Stop Illegal Entry Act
2025-264.plain: The House voted 226 to 197 to pass the Stop Illegal Entry Act. The bill would increase prison terms for certain non-citizens who illegally enter or reenter the United States, including mandatory minimum sentences of 5 or 10 years for some cases.

2025-265.name: Tabling a Resolution on a National Emergency
2025-265.plain: The House voted 200 to 198 to set aside a measure relating to the President's national emergency declared on July 30, 2025, which ends its consideration. Nearly all Republicans voted to set it aside, and nearly all Democrats voted to keep it alive.

2025-266.name: TRAVEL Act of 2025
2025-266.plain: The House passed the TRAVEL Act, 371 to 21. It would let the Department of Veterans Affairs assign a physician for up to one year to care for veterans at VA facilities in U.S. territories such as Guam, Puerto Rico, and American Samoa, and would require a relocation or retention bonus for those doctors.

2025-267.name: Procedural Vote on Seven Bills Including D.C. Juvenile Crime and Energy Measures
2025-267.plain: The House voted 213 to 207 to end debate and move toward final votes on seven bills, covering topics such as juvenile offender status and trial ages in Washington, D.C., police vehicle pursuits, energy projects, a coal advisory council, and border-crossing facilities for oil, gas, and electricity. This vote was on procedure, not on the bills themselves.

2025-268.name: Debate Rules for Seven D.C. and Energy Bills
2025-268.plain: The House voted 213 to 211 to approve the rules for debating seven measures, including changes to juvenile crime and D.C. courts and energy and coal policy. This was a procedural step that sets how long debate lasts and which amendments are allowed, not a final vote on those measures.

2025-269.name: Honoring Our Heroes Act of 2025
2025-269.plain: The House voted 413 to 0 to pass a bill requiring the Department of Veterans Affairs to run a two-year pilot program providing headstones or burial markers for certain veterans who died before November 1, 1990, if discharged under conditions other than dishonorable.

2025-27.name: Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act
2025-27.plain: The House voted 217 to 204 to pass a bill requiring that a baby born alive after an abortion or attempted abortion receive the same care as any other baby born alive at that age and be taken to a hospital, with criminal penalties for violations.

2025-270.name: D.C. Criminal Sentencing Limits Bill
2025-270.plain: The House passed a bill that would stop the District of Columbia government from changing criminal sentences already in effect, lower the age for youth offender treatment from 24 to 18, and require monthly public reporting of youth offender crime data. The vote was 240 to 179.

2025-271.name: Trying Children as Adults in D.C. Courts
2025-271.plain: The House passed a bill, 225 to 203, that would lower the age at which a child can be tried as an adult for certain crimes in the District of Columbia to 14, down from the current 15 or 16 depending on the offense.

2025-272.name: Procedural Vote on Funding Bill and Kirk Resolution
2025-272.plain: The House voted 213 to 207 to end debate and move toward a final vote on a rule that sets how two measures will be considered: a bill making continuing funding for fiscal year 2026, and a resolution honoring Charlie Kirk. Republicans voted yes and Democrats voted no.

2025-273.name: Debate Rules for Funding and Kirk Resolution
2025-273.plain: The House voted 216 to 210 to approve the rules for debating two measures: a bill to keep federal funding going for fiscal year 2026, and a resolution honoring Charlie Kirk. This vote set debate rules only and did not vote on either measure itself.

2025-274.name: District of Columbia Judicial Nominations Reform Act
2025-274.plain: The House passed the bill 218 to 211. It ends the commission that recommends D.C. Superior Court and Court of Appeals judges and has the President appoint their chief judges instead.

2025-275.name: D.C. Police Vehicle Pursuit Rules
2025-275.plain: The House voted 245 to 182 to pass a bill that would repeal current limits on police car chases in Washington, D.C., and generally require officers to pursue fleeing suspects unless specific exceptions apply.

2025-276.name: Motion to Table Censure of Rep. Ilhan Omar
2025-276.plain: The House voted 214 to 213 to set aside a resolution that would have censured Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota and removed her from the Education and Workforce and Budget committees. Setting it aside ends the resolution.

2025-277.name: Cross-Border Energy Infrastructure Act
2025-277.plain: The House voted 224 to 203 to pass a bill that would require federal approval for building energy pipelines and power lines across the U.S. border with Canada or Mexico, and would require congressional approval before the President could revoke certain such permits.

2025-278.name: National Coal Council Reestablishment Act
2025-278.plain: The House passed a bill, 217 to 209, to re-establish the National Coal Council, an advisory group that makes recommendations to the Department of Energy on coal, and to remove its requirement to be re-chartered every two years.

2025-279.name: GRID Power Act
2025-279.plain: The House passed the GRID Power Act, 216 to 206. The bill would direct federal energy regulators to speed up connecting dispatchable power projects, such as certain fossil fuel plants, to the electric grid by giving them higher priority in the connection line.

2025-28.name: Alaska Native Village Municipal Lands Restoration Act
2025-28.plain: The House passed a bill, 412 to 1, that removes the requirement for Alaska Native village corporations to transfer certain lands to Alaska to be held in trust for future municipal governments. It also lets village corporations regain title to those lands by formal resolution with village residents.

2025-280.name: Ending the Government Shutdown, Procedural Motion
2025-280.plain: The House voted on a procedural motion to send the bill back to committee, which failed 210 to 218. The bill would end the government shutdown that began October 1, 2025, by funding most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, and funding agriculture, military construction and veterans affairs, and legislative branch programs through the end of fiscal year 2026.

2025-281.name: Bill to End Government Shutdown and Extend Funding
2025-281.plain: The House passed a bill, 217 to 212, that ends the government shutdown that began October 1, 2025. It funds most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, and funds agriculture, military construction and veterans affairs, and legislative branch programs through the end of fiscal year 2026.

2025-282.name: Honoring Charlie Kirk's Life and Legacy
2025-282.plain: The House voted 310 to 58 to approve a resolution that condemns the assassination of Charlie Kirk and all forms of political violence, and honors his life, leadership, and legacy.

2025-283.name: Procedural Vote on Continuing Government Funding Bill
2025-283.plain: The House voted 216 to 213 to end debate and move to a final vote on a Senate change to a bill that would keep government funding going into 2026. This was a procedural step, not the final vote on the bill itself.

2025-284.name: Debate Rules for a Government Funding Bill
2025-284.plain: The House voted 213 to 209 to approve the rules for debating a Senate change to a bill that provides continuing funding for government agencies in fiscal year 2026. The vote set how long debate would last and which amendments could be considered, rather than deciding the bill itself.

2025-285.name: Bill to End the Government Shutdown
2025-285.plain: The House voted 222 to 209 to accept the Senate's changes to this bill, which ends the government shutdown that began October 1, 2025. It provides funding for most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, and funds agriculture, military construction and veterans affairs, and legislative branch programs through the end of fiscal 2026.

2025-286.name: Vehicular Terrorism Prevention and Mitigation Act
2025-286.plain: The House voted 400 to 15 to pass a bill requiring the Department of Homeland Security to report to Congress on preventing and responding to terrorism carried out with vehicles, including threats, vulnerable locations, and technology recommendations.

2025-287.name: Cyber Resilience Against State-Sponsored Threats Act
2025-287.plain: The House passed the bill 402 to 8, using a fast-track process that needed two-thirds approval. It would create a joint government task force, led by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to coordinate responses to Chinese state-sponsored hackers, including Volt Typhoon, and require annual reports to Congress for six years.

2025-288.name: Motion to Set Aside Censure of Rep. García
2025-288.plain: The House voted on whether to set aside a resolution expressing disapproval of Representative Chuy García of Illinois. The motion failed 206 to 211, so the resolution stays alive.

2025-289.name: Epstein Files Transparency Act
2025-289.plain: The House voted 427 to 1 to pass a bill requiring the Justice Department to publish its unclassified records about the investigation and prosecution of Jeffrey Epstein, with some information such as victims' personal details withheld.

2025-29.name: Nutria Eradication and Control Reauthorization Act
2025-29.plain: The House passed a bill extending through 2030 a federal program that lets the Interior Department give states money to remove invasive nutria, semi-aquatic rodents, and restore marsh they have damaged. The vote was 361 in favor and 56 against.

2025-290.name: Procedural Vote on Multiple Measures Including Energy and D.C. Policing
2025-290.plain: The House voted 217 to 211 to end debate and move toward a final vote on several measures, including bills on energy, natural gas, and D.C. policing. This was a procedural step, not a vote on the measures themselves.

2025-291.name: Debate Rules for Several Measures
2025-291.plain: The House voted 217 to 210 to approve the rules for debating several measures, including bills on Alaska and Buffalo land-use plans, natural gas trade, and District of Columbia policing and bail. This was a procedural step that sets how and when those measures will be debated, not a final vote on them.

2025-292.name: Disapproval of Representative Chuy García's Behavior
2025-292.plain: The House voted 236 to 183 to approve a resolution expressing disapproval of Representative Jesús "Chuy" García of Illinois's behavior. Nearly all Republicans and 23 Democrats voted yes, and the other Democrats voted no.

2025-293.name: Motion to Refer Censure of Delegate Plaskett
2025-293.plain: The House voted on whether to send a measure to censure Delegate Stacey Plaskett and remove her from an intelligence committee over her conduct with Jeffrey Epstein during a hearing to a committee, which would have set it aside. The motion failed, 213 to 214, so the measure stays on the House floor.

2025-294.name: Buffalo Field Office Coal Leasing Rule Disapproval
2025-294.plain: The House passed a measure, 214 to 212, to overturn a Bureau of Land Management rule that had made federal coal in the Buffalo Field Office area in Wyoming unavailable for future leasing. The measure would require the agency to follow its 2015 land plan, under which coal could be leased.

2025-295.name: Arctic Refuge Oil and Gas Leasing Rule
2025-295.plain: The House voted 217 to 209 to pass a resolution that cancels a December 2024 Bureau of Land Management decision on oil and gas leasing in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. If enacted, it would open land there to oil and gas leasing.

2025-296.name: Alaska Petroleum Reserve Oil and Gas Plan
2025-296.plain: The House voted 216 to 209 to pass a measure that would cancel a 2022 federal plan for the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska and restore the 2020 plan, which opens more of the area to oil and gas leasing.

2025-297.name: Censuring Delegate Stacey Plaskett
2025-297.plain: The House voted on whether to censure Delegate Stacey Plaskett and remove her from the Intelligence Committee over her conduct with Jeffrey Epstein during a hearing. The measure failed, 209 in favor to 214 against.

2025-298.name: District of Columbia Cash Bail Reform Act of 2025
2025-298.plain: The House passed a bill requiring people charged with violent or dangerous crimes in Washington, D.C. to be held in jail before trial, and requiring cash bail for release in certain public safety cases. The vote was 237 in favor to 179 against.

2025-299.name: Repeal of D.C. Policing Reform Act
2025-299.plain: The House passed a bill, 233 to 190, to repeal a 2022 D.C. Council law on policing, which had limited certain neck restraints by officers, set body camera procedures, and expanded access to police discipline records. The repeal would restore any laws that the 2022 act had changed or removed.

2025-3.name: House Rules for the 119th Congress
2025-3.plain: The House voted 216 to 210 to end debate and move to a final vote on the rules that will govern the House for the 119th Congress. The rules set the chamber's procedures and include changes such as eliminating the House Office of Diversity and Inclusion.

2025-30.name: Rule Vote on HALT Fentanyl Act
2025-30.plain: The House voted 212 to 208 to end debate and move ahead to a final vote on the HALT Fentanyl Act, which would change how fentanyl-related substances are scheduled under the Controlled Substances Act. This was a procedural vote, not a vote on the bill itself.

2025-300.name: Support and Outreach for Homeland Security Preparedness Grants
2025-300.plain: The House passed a bill, 380 to 45, requiring the Federal Emergency Management Agency to provide outreach, technical help, and yearly surveys to local governments and other groups about grants for protecting communities from terrorist attacks. It also requires reports to Congress on how the agency carries it out.

2025-301.name: Repeal of Senate Office Data Lawsuit Authority
2025-301.plain: The House voted 426 to 0 to pass a bill that would remove the power of a Senator to sue the federal government over improper access to Senate office data by internet providers or the Senate Sergeant at Arms.

2025-302.name: Censure of Representative Cory Mills
2025-302.plain: The House voted 310 to 103 to send a measure to remove Representative Cory Mills of Florida from two committees, which sets the measure aside instead of deciding it on the House floor. The measure would censure him and remove him from the Armed Services and Foreign Affairs committees.

2025-303.name: REFINER Act (Petrochemical Refinery Report)
2025-303.plain: The House passed the REFINER Act, 230 to 176. It would require the Department of Energy to have the National Petroleum Council publish a report on U.S. petrochemical refineries, covering their role in energy security, opportunities and risks for expanding them, government actions that have reduced their capacity, and recommendations to increase it.

2025-304.name: Natural Gas Export and Import Approval Changes
2025-304.plain: The House passed a bill, 217 to 188, that would remove some federal rules on importing and exporting natural gas and move approval of related facilities to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. Republicans voted for it and Democrats mostly voted against it.

2025-305.name: Resolution Denouncing Socialism
2025-305.plain: The House approved a resolution denouncing socialism and opposing the adoption of socialist policies in the United States, by a vote of 285 to 98.

2025-306.name: Social Security Child Protection Act
2025-306.plain: The House passed a bill, 386 to 0, that would require the Social Security Administration to issue a new Social Security number to a child under 14 whose card was lost or stolen in the mail.

2025-307.name: No New Burma Funds Act
2025-307.plain: The House passed the No New Burma Funds Act by 385 to 0. It would require the U.S. representative at the World Bank's main lending arm to push for keeping the pause on loans and new financing to Burma, unless the Treasury Department finds that is not in the national interest.

2025-308.name: Procedural Vote on Six Bills
2025-308.plain: The House voted 210 to 205 to end debate and move to a final vote on six bills covering college athletes' name and likeness rights, Chinese government funding of schools, parental notice of foreign influence in schools, a small business regulatory budget, and a Red Tape Hotline for burdensome agency rules. This vote did not decide the bills themselves.

2025-309.name: Debate Rules for Six House Bills
2025-309.plain: The House voted 210 to 209 to approve the rules for debating six bills, covering college athlete pay rights, limits on Chinese government funding for public schools, parental notice of foreign influence in schools, small business regulation, and a hotline for burdensome agency rules. This was a procedural step that sets debate time and allowed amendments, not a vote on the bills themselves.

2025-31.name: Debate Rules for the HALT Fentanyl Act
2025-31.plain: The House voted 215 to 208 to approve the rules for debating a bill that would place fentanyl-related substances under the Controlled Substances Act. This was a procedural step that sets how the debate on the bill will proceed.

2025-310.name: Small Business Regulatory Reduction Act of 2025
2025-310.plain: The House passed this bill 223 to 190. It would require the Small Business Administration to keep the yearly cost of federal rules on small businesses at zero or less.

2025-311.name: DUMP Red Tape Act
2025-311.plain: The House voted to pass the DUMP Red Tape Act, 269 to 146. The bill would require the Small Business Administration's Office of Advocacy to keep running a hotline where small businesses can report burdensome federal rules and to report yearly on those complaints.

2025-312.name: Limiting Chinese Government Funding in Schools
2025-312.plain: The House passed a bill that would bar public elementary and secondary schools from accepting funds or contracts from the Chinese government or the Chinese Communist Party, as a condition of receiving federal education funds, and would require schools to disclose any such foreign funding to the Department of Education. The vote was 242 in favor and 176 against.

2025-313.name: PROTECT Our Kids Act
2025-313.plain: The House voted 247 to 164 to pass the PROTECT Our Kids Act. It would bar federal education funding for any elementary or secondary school that has ties to Chinese government-funded programs, such as Confucius Institutes or Confucius Classrooms, with some waivers allowed.

2025-314.name: Transparency in Reporting of Adversarial Contributions to Education Act
2025-314.plain: The House voted 247 to 166 to pass this bill. It would require schools receiving federal education funds to tell parents they can request information about foreign-government funding, curriculum materials, and staff pay tied to that funding.

2025-315.name: Secure Rural Schools Reauthorization Act
