2025-315.plain: The House voted 399 to 5 to pass a bill that extends payments to states and counties with federal land for schools, roads and other local services, and provides payments that lapsed for 2024 and 2025. The bill was passed under a fast-track process requiring two-thirds support.

2025-316.name: Deadline for Wildlife Conservation Plan Approval
2025-316.plain: The House passed, 400 to 0, a bill that would require the Interior Department to approve a state's wildlife conservation plan within 180 days of its submission if the plan meets requirements. If the deadline is missed, the plan would be automatically approved and funds would be set aside for that state.

2025-317.name: Rule Package for Several Bills
2025-317.plain: The House voted 216 to 210 to pass a procedural step that ends debate on a set of bills and moves them to a final vote. This was not a vote on the bills themselves. Votes split along party lines.

2025-318.name: Debate Rules for Several Energy, Water and Veterans Bills
2025-318.plain: The House voted 215 to 211 to approve the rules for debating several bills on water pollution, electricity supply, natural gas reviews, investment funds and a veteran's remains. This was a procedural step that sets how long debate lasts and which changes are allowed, not a vote on the bills themselves.

2025-319.name: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026
2025-319.plain: The House voted against sending the defense policy bill back to committee, so it moved on to the final vote. The bill sets policies and authorizes funding levels for military programs, equipment, personnel, and related national security activities for fiscal year 2026.

2025-32.name: HALT Fentanyl Act Amendment
2025-32.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the HALT Fentanyl Act, which would permanently place fentanyl-related substances as a class into the most restricted drug category under federal law. The amendment was rejected, 182 in favor to 226 opposed.

2025-320.name: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026
2025-320.plain: The House passed the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, 312 to 112. The bill sets policies and authorizes programs for military, defense, and related national security activities for 2026, including weapons purchases, troop levels, and military construction.

2025-321.name: Federal Workers' Labor Rights Executive Order
2025-321.plain: The House voted 222 to 200 to bring up a bill that would cancel a 2025 executive order removing certain federal agencies from federal employee union and collective bargaining rules. The vote was to move the bill to the House floor for debate rather than leave it in committee.

2025-322.name: Motion to Table Impeachment of President Trump
2025-322.plain: The House voted 237 to 140 to set aside a resolution to impeach President Donald Trump, which would have charged him with abusing presidential power by calling for the execution of members of Congress and by trying to intimidate federal judges. Setting it aside ends the measure.

2025-323.name: State Planning for Reliable Electricity Act
2025-323.plain: The House passed a bill, 218 to 207, that would ask state regulators to consider requiring electric utilities to plan for keeping enough reliable power available over the next 10 years, including backup fuel for at least 30 days of generation.

2025-324.name: Electric Supply Chain Act
2025-324.plain: The House passed the Electric Supply Chain Act, 267 to 159. The bill would require the Department of Energy to regularly assess the supply of components needed to generate and move electricity and report its findings and recommendations to Congress.

2025-325.name: Amendment to the Capital Formation Act
2025-325.plain: The House rejected an amendment, 374 to 54, that would have changed a bill to make it easier for closed-end funds to invest more in private investment funds. The bill would bar the Securities and Exchange Commission from limiting the sale or listing of such funds' securities.

2025-326.name: Amendment to Capital Formation Act
2025-326.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the Incentivizing New Ventures and Economic Strength Through Capital Formation Act of 2025, which would stop the Securities and Exchange Commission from limiting the sale or listing of certain closed-end funds that invest in private investment funds. The amendment was rejected, 211 in favor to 219 against.

2025-327.name: Amendment to the Capital Formation Act
2025-327.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the Incentivizing New Ventures and Economic Strength Through Capital Formation Act of 2025, and it failed, 214 to 215. The amendment would stop the Securities and Exchange Commission from limiting the sale or listing of shares in certain closed-end funds that invest in private investment funds.

2025-328.name: Capital Formation Act of 2025
2025-328.plain: The House passed a bill, 302 to 123, that would stop the Securities and Exchange Commission from limiting the sale or listing of closed-end funds that invest in private investment funds. Republicans voted for it and Democrats were divided.

2025-329.name: Limits on Clean Water Act Protections
2025-329.plain: The House voted on whether to send the PERMIT Act back to committee, and the motion failed 210 to 216. The bill would narrow the Clean Water Act by excluding waste treatment systems, groundwater, certain seasonal streams, and some farmland, among other features.

2025-33.name: HALT Fentanyl Act
2025-33.plain: The House passed the HALT Fentanyl Act, 312 to 108. The bill would permanently place fentanyl-related substances as a class under the strictest federal drug category, with the same penalties used for fentanyl analogues.

2025-330.name: PERMIT Act Clean Water Changes
2025-330.plain: The House passed the PERMIT Act, 221 to 205. The bill would narrow which waters are covered by the Clean Water Act by excluding certain features, such as waste treatment systems, groundwater, and some cropland, from the definition of navigable waters.

2025-331.name: Debate Rules for Federal Worker Union Bill
2025-331.plain: The House voted 232 to 194 to approve the rules for debating a bill that would cancel a 2025 executive order removing certain federal agencies from federal worker union and collective bargaining requirements. The vote set debate rules only and was not a vote on the bill itself.

2025-332.name: Protect America's Workforce Act
2025-332.plain: The House passed the Protect America's Workforce Act, 231 to 195. The bill would cancel a March 2025 executive order that removed certain federal agencies from federal workers' collective bargaining rights, and keep existing union contracts in effect through their stated terms.

2025-333.name: Motion to Recommit Pipeline Review Bill
2025-333.plain: The House voted on whether to send the Improving Interagency Coordination for Pipeline Reviews Act back to committee, and the motion failed 194 to 204. The bill would speed environmental reviews for certain natural gas pipelines and LNG terminals by making the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission the lead agency for those reviews.

2025-334.name: Faster Environmental Reviews for Natural Gas Pipelines
2025-334.plain: The House voted to pass a bill that would speed up environmental reviews for certain natural gas pipelines and liquefied natural gas terminals by making the federal energy regulatory commission the lead agency for those reviews. The bill passed 213 to 184.

2025-335.name: Congressional Award Program Reauthorization Act
2025-335.plain: The House voted to pass a bill extending the Congressional Award Board, which gives medals to young people ages 14 to 23 for achievement in public service, personal development, and physical fitness, through 2028 and removing a rule about the medals' metal. The bill passed, 370 to 22.

2025-336.name: Transfer of Forest Service Land to Perry County, Arkansas
2025-336.plain: The House voted 388 to 0 to pass a bill directing the federal Forest Service to give about one acre of land to Perry County, Arkansas, at the county's request, for public uses such as education and youth programs. The county would pay the conveyance costs.

2025-337.name: Rule Package for Six Bills on Environment, Energy, Wolves, and Child Trafficking
2025-337.plain: The House voted 215 to 207 to end debate and move to a final vote on a procedural package covering six bills, including changes to environmental reviews, hardrock mine sites, gray wolf protections, electric grid reliability, power plant retirement notices, and child trafficking efforts. The vote was not on the bills themselves.

2025-338.name: Debate Rules for Six Measures
2025-338.plain: The House voted 215 to 209 to approve the rules for debating six measures, covering environmental reviews, mining sites, gray wolf protections, electric grid oversight, power plant retirements, and child trafficking. This was a procedural step, not a vote on the measures themselves.

2025-339.name: Kayla Hamilton Act Referral to Committee
2025-339.plain: The House voted 208 to 218 on whether to send the Kayla Hamilton Act back to committee, and the motion failed. The bill would require the Department of Health and Human Services to consider more information when placing unaccompanied migrant children, including danger and flight risk, and to bar placing children with sponsors who are in the country unlawfully.

2025-34.name: Protecting American Energy Production Act
2025-34.plain: The House voted 205 to 207 on whether to send this bill back to committee, and the motion failed. The bill would stop the President from declaring a moratorium on fracking unless Congress approves it.

2025-340.name: Kayla Hamilton Act
2025-340.plain: The House passed the Kayla Hamilton Act, 225 to 201. It would require the Department of Health and Human Services to consider danger, community risk and flight risk when placing unaccompanied migrant children, and to share sponsor household information with Homeland Security.

2025-341.name: Power Plant Reliability Act Committee Referral
2025-341.plain: The House voted 207 to 218 against sending the Power Plant Reliability Act back to committee, so the bill moved on to a final vote. The bill would let federal regulators order a power plant to stay open for up to five years if its closure would make the power grid unreliable, and would exempt compliance actions from certain environmental laws.

2025-342.name: Power Plant Reliability Act
2025-342.plain: The House passed a bill, 222 to 202, that lets federal energy regulators order a power plant to stay open for up to five years if its closure would make the electricity system unreliable. Plant owners would have to give five years' notice before planned retirements.

2025-343.name: Rules Package on Health Insurance, Medicaid, and Environmental Review Bills
2025-343.plain: The House voted 204 to 203 to end debate and move toward a final vote on a set of bills, covering health insurance access, Medicaid funding for gender transition procedures for minors, penalties for genital mutilation and chemical castration of minors, and changes to the environmental review process. The vote itself was procedural and did not decide the bills.

2025-344.name: Debate Rules for Four Bills
2025-344.plain: The House voted 213 to 209 to approve rules for debating four bills, on health insurance access, Medicaid funding for minors' gender transition procedures, genital mutilation and chemical castration of minors, and environmental review. This was a procedural step, not a vote on the bills themselves.

2025-345.name: Ending Military Hostilities with Designated Western Hemisphere Terrorist Groups
2025-345.plain: The House voted on a non-binding request asking the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities with terrorist groups in the Western Hemisphere that the President has designated, unless Congress has declared war or authorized the use of force. The request failed, 210 in favor to 216 against.

2025-346.name: U.S. Military Action in Venezuela
2025-346.plain: The House voted on a resolution directing the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities within or against Venezuela unless Congress has declared war or authorized the use of military force for that purpose. The resolution failed, 211 in favor to 213 against.

2025-347.name: Reliable Power Act
2025-347.plain: The House passed the Reliable Power Act, 225 to 203. It would require federal agencies to get review from federal energy regulators before finalizing rules that affect power generation, if the grid is found to lack enough electricity to stay reliable.

2025-348.name: Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act
2025-348.plain: The House voted on whether to send the Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act back to committee, a last step before a final vote on the bill. The motion failed, 210 in favor and 218 against, so the bill moved on toward a final vote.

2025-349.name: Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act
2025-349.plain: The House voted 216 to 211 to pass the Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act. Nearly all Republicans voted yes, and nearly all Democrats voted no.

2025-35.name: Protecting American Energy Production Act
2025-35.plain: The House voted 226 to 188 to pass a bill that would stop the President from halting hydraulic fracturing, commonly called fracking, unless Congress first approves such a halt. It also states that Congress believes states should keep control over fracking regulation on state and private lands.

2025-350.name: Protect Children's Innocence Act Committee Referral
2025-350.plain: The House rejected sending the Protect Children's Innocence Act back to committee, 210 to 218, keeping it on track for a final vote. The bill would make it a federal crime to give minors gender-affirming care, with exceptions, and would broaden the federal ban on female genital mutilation.

2025-351.name: Protect Children's Innocence Act
2025-351.plain: The House voted 216 to 211 to pass a bill making it a federal crime to provide gender-affirming medical treatments, such as hormones or surgery, to minors, with penalties of a fine, up to 10 years in prison, or both. It also expands the existing federal ban on female genital mutilation to cover anyone who facilitates or consents to it.

2025-352.name: SPEED Act Amendment on Environmental Reviews
2025-352.plain: The House considered an amendment to the SPEED Act, a bill that would limit and speed up federal environmental reviews under the National Environmental Policy Act. The amendment was rejected, 205 in favor to 220 against.

2025-353.name: SPEED Act Amendment on Environmental Reviews
2025-353.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the SPEED Act, a bill that would limit and speed up environmental reviews of major federal actions under NEPA. The amendment was rejected, 208 to 214.

2025-354.name: SPEED Act Amendment on Environmental Reviews
2025-354.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the SPEED Act, a bill that would limit environmental reviews of major federal actions under NEPA and speed up that review process. The amendment was rejected, 204 for and 217 against.

2025-355.name: Motion to Send the SPEED Act Back to Committee
2025-355.plain: The House voted on whether to send the SPEED Act back to committee, which would have delayed a final vote. The motion failed, 206 to 211. The bill would limit the scope of federal environmental reviews under NEPA and speed up the review process.

2025-356.name: SPEED Act on Environmental Permitting
2025-356.plain: The House passed the SPEED Act, 221 to 196. The bill would limit when federal agencies must conduct environmental reviews under NEPA, speed up those reviews, and restrict court challenges to them.

2025-357.name: Mining Regulatory Clarity Act
2025-357.plain: The House voted 205 to 213 against sending the Mining Regulatory Clarity Act back to committee, so the bill moved on to a final vote. The bill would let mining companies use federal land for waste disposal and related work, and it creates a fund for cleaning up abandoned hardrock mines.

2025-358.name: Mining Regulatory Clarity Act
2025-358.plain: The House passed the Mining Regulatory Clarity Act, 219 to 198. It would let mining operators use federal land for activities like waste disposal, and it would set up an Abandoned Hardrock Mine Fund for cleaning up old mines.

2025-359.name: Pet and Livestock Protection Act Recommittal Vote
2025-359.plain: The House rejected a motion to send the Pet and Livestock Protection Act back to committee, by 204 to 213, which means the bill moved on toward a final vote. The bill would direct the Interior Department to reissue a rule removing gray wolf protections under the Endangered Species Act and bar judicial review of that reissued rule.

2025-36.name: China Exchange Rate Transparency Act
2025-36.plain: The House passed the China Exchange Rate Transparency Act, 388 to 7. The bill would direct the U.S. representative at the International Monetary Fund to push for more openness from China about its currency exchange rates, and the requirement would expire after seven years unless China meets certain conditions sooner.

2025-360.name: Gray Wolf Protections Removal Bill
2025-360.plain: The House passed the Pet and Livestock Protection Act, 211 to 204. The bill would direct the government to reissue a rule removing federal endangered-species protections for the gray wolf in most of the lower 48 states and bar court review of that rule.

2025-361.name: Motion to Send Medicaid Gender Transition Bill Back to Committee
2025-361.plain: The House voted on whether to send the Do No Harm in Medicaid Act back to committee, and the motion failed 204 to 212. The bill would bar federal Medicaid payment for gender transition procedures for people under 18, with exceptions such as treatment for early puberty, genetic or chromosomal disorders, and procedures to prevent death.

2025-362.name: Medicaid Payment Limits for Minors' Gender Transition Procedures
2025-362.plain: The House voted to pass the Do No Harm in Medicaid Act, 215 to 201. The bill would bar federal Medicaid payment for certain gender transition procedures for people under 18, with exceptions for early puberty, genetic or chromosomal conditions, reversing prior procedures, and preventing imminent death or serious bodily harm.

2025-37.name: Extending Deadline for Company Ownership Reports
2025-37.plain: The House voted 408 to 0 to pass a bill that gives certain companies formed or registered before January 1, 2024, until January 1, 2026, instead of January 1, 2025, to report their beneficial ownership information to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network.

2025-38.name: Procedural Vote on Midnight Rules Bill
2025-38.plain: The House voted 210 to 184 to end debate on a procedural step and move toward a final vote on a bill about speeding up congressional reviews of late-term federal rules. It was not a vote on the bill itself. Republicans voted yes and Democrats voted no.

2025-39.name: Debate Rules for a Midnight Rules Disapproval Bill
2025-39.plain: The House approved, 216 to 205, the rules that set how long debate would last and which changes could be offered on a bill about allowing certain end-of-term federal rules to be reviewed together. The vote was on the debate rules only, not on the bill itself.

2025-4.name: Rules for the 119th Congress
2025-4.plain: The House rejected a motion to send the House rules for the 119th Congress back to committee, by a vote of 209 to 214, so the rules moved toward a final vote. The rules set how the House operates, including changes to voting procedures and the elimination of the House Office of Diversity and Inclusion.

2025-40.name: Midnight Rules Relief Act
2025-40.plain: The House voted on whether to send the Midnight Rules Relief Act back to committee, which would have delayed the bill. The motion failed, 205 to 213. The bill would let Congress disapprove multiple regulations at once when they were submitted during the final year of a President's term.

2025-41.name: Midnight Rules Relief Act
2025-41.plain: The House voted 212 to 208 to pass a bill letting Congress reject several federal regulations at once, when they were submitted late in a President's final year in office.

2025-42.name: Agent Raul Gonzalez Officer Safety Act
2025-42.plain: The House passed this bill 264 to 155. It would make it a federal crime to drive within 100 miles of the U.S. border while fleeing a Border Patrol agent or a law enforcement officer working with them, with a mandatory minimum prison term if someone dies or is seriously hurt. Non-citizens convicted under it would be barred from staying in the U.S. and from asylum.

2025-43.name: Barring Financial Fraudsters from Small Business Aid
2025-43.plain: The House voted 405 to 0 to pass a bill that would bar people convicted of certain financial crimes tied to COVID-19 business loans and grants from receiving Small Business Administration assistance, including businesses they own or run. The bill was considered under a fast-track process requiring two-thirds support.

2025-44.name: Small Business Advocacy Improvements Act
2025-44.plain: The House passed a bill that expands the Small Business Administration's Office of Advocacy to examine small businesses' role in the international economy and to represent their interests before foreign governments and international groups. The vote was 396 in favor and 15 against.

2025-45.name: SPUR Act on Small Business Contracting
2025-45.plain: The House passed the SPUR Act, 384 to 25, through a fast-track process that required two-thirds support. The bill would require federal agencies to count, on their annual small business contracting scorecard, how many businesses owned by service-disabled veterans, HUBZone businesses, socially and economically disadvantaged individuals, or women receive a first-time prime contract.

2025-46.name: Rules for Three Measures on Water Heaters, Methane Fees, and Budget
2025-46.plain: The House voted 216 to 210 to end debate and move to a final vote on a package covering three measures: a rule on gas water heater efficiency standards, a rule on fees for methane emissions from oil and gas facilities, and a budget plan for 2025 and later years. This vote was procedural and did not decide the measures themselves.

2025-47.name: Debate Rules for Three Measures
2025-47.plain: The House voted 217 to 211 to approve the rules for debating three measures: a disapproval of a Department of Energy water heater standard, a disapproval of an EPA oil and gas emissions charge rule, and a federal budget plan for 2025. This was a procedural step that sets how the debate will run, not a vote on the measures themselves.

2025-48.name: DOE and SBA Research Act
2025-48.plain: The House passed a bill requiring the Department of Energy and the Small Business Administration to agree to work together on research and development, including small businesses where appropriate, and to report on their collaborative achievements. The vote was 427 in favor and 3 against.

2025-49.name: Rural Small Business Resilience Act
2025-49.plain: The House passed a bill, 415 to 8, requiring the Small Business Administration to make sure people in rural areas with declared disasters fully get disaster assistance, including targeted outreach to them.

2025-5.name: Rules for the 119th Congress
2025-5.plain: The House voted 215 to 209 to approve a resolution setting the House's operating rules for the 119th Congress. It keeps most of the previous rules with changes, including limits on removing the Speaker and on waiving the germaneness rule for amendments.

2025-50.name: Congressional Budget Plan for Fiscal Years 2025–2034
2025-50.plain: The House voted 217 to 215 to approve a budget resolution setting federal spending, revenue, and deficit targets for fiscal year 2025 and projected levels through 2034. It also directs House committees to draft legislation that would change the deficit and raise the federal debt limit.

2025-51.name: Medal of Honor Act
2025-51.plain: The House passed the Medal of Honor Act 424 to 0. It would raise the monthly special pension for living Medal of Honor recipients, bar the VA from adding an extra inflation increase in a year when the pension was already raised, and extend until January 31, 2033 the $90 monthly cap on pensions paid to veterans without a spouse or child who live in Medicaid nursing homes.

2025-52.name: Repeal of Oil and Gas Methane Charge
2025-52.plain: The House passed a measure to cancel an EPA rule that set up a yearly charge on oil and gas facilities for excess methane and other greenhouse gas emissions. The vote was 220 in favor and 206 against.

2025-53.name: Energy Efficiency Standards for Gas Water Heaters
2025-53.plain: The House passed a measure, 221 to 198, to cancel a federal Energy Department rule that set stricter energy efficiency standards for gas-fired instantaneous water heaters. Those standards were issued in December 2024.

2025-54.name: Safe and Smart Federal Purchasing Act
2025-54.plain: The House voted 417 to 0 to pass a bill requiring the Office of Management and Budget to review whether certain federal buying rules, which favor the lowest-priced acceptable supplier, have created national security risks, and to report its findings to Congress.

2025-55.name: Mail Traffic Deaths Reporting Act
2025-55.plain: The House passed a bill requiring the Postal Service to track and publicly report deaths and injuries from crashes involving mail vehicles, with employees and contractors reporting such crashes within three days. The vote was 402 in favor and 16 against.

2025-56.name: Rules for Three Federal Rule Disapproval Measures
2025-56.plain: The House voted 196 to 187 to set the rules for debate on three measures that would block federal rules on home appliance energy labeling, rubber tire factory air pollution, and protection of marine archaeological sites. This was a procedural vote to end debate and move to a final vote, not a vote on the measures themselves.

2025-57.name: Debate Rules for Three Federal Rule Disapprovals
2025-57.plain: The House voted 211 to 209 to approve the rules for debating three measures that would overturn federal agency regulations: one on appliance energy standards, one on rubber tire manufacturing air pollution, and one on protecting marine archaeological sites. This vote set debate rules only and did not decide the measures themselves.

2025-58.name: Rubber Tire Manufacturing Air Pollution Rule Repeal
2025-58.plain: The House voted 216 to 202 to pass a measure that would cancel an Environmental Protection Agency rule setting limits on hazardous air pollutants from the rubber processing part of tire manufacturing. Nearly all Republicans voted yes, and nearly all Democrats voted no.

2025-59.name: Overturning Energy Rules for Appliances
2025-59.plain: The House voted to pass a measure to cancel a Department of Energy rule that updated certification, labeling, and enforcement requirements for certain appliances and industrial equipment, such as washing machines, dishwashers, and computer room air conditioners. The vote was 222 in favor and 203 against.

2025-6.name: Laken Riley Act
2025-6.plain: The House passed a bill, 264 to 159, that requires detaining certain non-citizens who are arrested for burglary, theft, larceny, or shoplifting and lack legal status, and lets states sue the federal government over certain immigration enforcement decisions that cause them harm.

2025-60.name: Censure of Representative Al Green
2025-60.plain: The House voted on whether to set aside a resolution to censure Representative Al Green of Texas. The motion failed, 209 to 211, so the resolution stays under consideration.

2025-61.name: Ocean Archaeology Rule Disapproval
2025-61.plain: The House passed a measure cancelling a federal rule that required oil and gas companies to submit archaeological reports, with exceptions, for offshore exploration plans. The rule would be replaced by earlier regulations that required such reports only when there was reason to believe archaeological remains might be present. The vote was 221 to 202.

2025-62.name: Censuring Representative Al Green
2025-62.plain: The House voted 224 to 198 to approve a resolution censuring Representative Al Green of Texas. Nearly all Republicans voted yes, and nearly all Democrats voted no.

2025-63.name: Subterranean Border Defense Act
2025-63.plain: The House voted 402 to 1 to pass the Subterranean Border Defense Act. It would require U.S. Customs and Border Protection to report every year, instead of once, on its plan to counter illegal cross-border tunnels.

2025-64.name: Research Security and Accountability in DHS Act
2025-64.plain: The House voted 410 to 1 to pass a bill requiring the Department of Homeland Security to set a department-wide policy for protecting sensitive research from unauthorized access, and requiring the Government Accountability Office to report on the department's compliance with a 2021 presidential memorandum on disclosures for government-funded research.

2025-65.name: Emerging Border Technologies Act
2025-65.plain: The House passed a bill, 406 to 9, requiring the U.S. Customs and Border Protection agency to create a plan for identifying and using new technologies to improve border security, and to set up teams to research commercial technologies for that purpose. The plan is due to Congress within 180 days.

2025-66.name: Procedural Vote on Digital Asset Rule and Other Bills
2025-66.plain: The House voted 216 to 212 to end debate and move toward a final vote on a package of measures. The package covers a rule on how brokers report digital asset sales, an extension of the time limit for fraud cases under certain unemployment programs, and a temporary government funding extension. This vote was not on the measures themselves.

2025-67.name: Debate Rules for Several Bills
2025-67.plain: The House voted 216 to 214 to approve the rules for debating several measures, including one on IRS reporting for digital asset sales, one extending the fraud statute of limitations for certain unemployment programs, and one on continuing government funding. This was a procedural step, not a vote on those measures themselves.

2025-68.name: Pandemic Unemployment Fraud Enforcement Act
2025-68.plain: The House passed a bill giving federal prosecutors and civil enforcers 10 years, instead of 5, to bring fraud cases tied to pandemic-era unemployment programs. It also cancels certain unused anti-fraud funds that were provided in the 2021 American Rescue Plan Act. The vote was 295 in favor and 127 against.

2025-69.name: Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
2025-69.plain: The House voted on whether to send this bill back to committee, and the motion failed 213 to 216. The bill would keep most federal programs funded at 2024 levels through the end of fiscal 2025 and extend several expiring health programs and authorities.

2025-7.name: Sanctions on Foreign Aides to the International Criminal Court
2025-7.plain: The House voted 243 to 140 to pass a bill that would require sanctions on foreign people who help the International Criminal Court investigate or prosecute certain individuals, and would cancel funding for that court.

2025-70.name: Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
2025-70.plain: The House voted 217 to 213 to pass a bill that keeps federal agencies funded at FY2024 levels for the rest of 2025, preventing a shutdown, and extends various expiring health programs, including Medicare and Medicaid provisions.

2025-71.name: Reporting Rule for Digital Asset Brokers
2025-71.plain: The House voted 292 to 132 to pass a measure that would cancel an IRS rule requiring certain decentralized finance (DeFi) services that help with digital asset sales to report information about those sales to the IRS.

2025-72.name: Cost-Share Accountability Act of 2025
2025-72.plain: The House passed the bill 405 to 0. It would require the Department of Energy to report on how it uses its power to reduce or remove required non-federal cost shares for certain federally funded energy research and development projects, starting within 120 days and then at least quarterly.

2025-73.name: DOE and USDA Interagency Research Act
2025-73.plain: The House voted to pass the DOE and USDA Interagency Research Act, 372 to 35, sending it forward. The bill requires the Energy and Agriculture departments to run joint research projects, chosen through a competitive review, on topics such as artificial intelligence, biofuels, and wildfire prevention.

2025-74.name: IMPACT Act: Low-Emissions Cement, Concrete and Asphalt
2025-74.plain: The House passed the IMPACT Act 350 to 73 under a fast-track process requiring two-thirds support. It would have the Department of Energy run a seven-year program funding projects to develop cleaner-producing cement, concrete and asphalt.

2025-75.name: Procedural Vote on Energy Rules and Foreign Gifts Bill
2025-75.plain: The House voted 215 to 208 to end debate and move to a final vote on a package covering two Energy Department rules on coolers and freezers and a bill about foreign gifts and contracts at colleges. This vote was procedural and did not decide the measures themselves.

2025-76.name: Debate Rules for Energy Rules and Foreign Gifts Bill
2025-76.plain: The House voted 214 to 207 to approve the rules for debating three measures: two to overturn Energy Department efficiency standards for walk-in coolers and freezers and for commercial refrigerators, and one bill to strengthen disclosure of foreign gifts and contracts at colleges. This was a procedural step, not a vote on the measures themselves.

2025-77.name: Energy Standards for Walk-In Coolers and Freezers
2025-77.plain: The House passed a measure to cancel new, stricter energy efficiency rules for walk-in coolers and freezers, including limits on daily energy use for their non-display doors. The vote was 203 in favor and 182 against.

2025-78.name: Energy Efficiency Standards for Commercial Refrigerators
2025-78.plain: The House voted 214 to 193 to pass a measure that cancels new, stricter energy efficiency standards for commercial refrigerators, freezers, and refrigerator-freezers, so that equipment no longer has to meet them by 2029.

2025-79.name: DETERRENT Act Amendment
2025-79.plain: The House rejected an amendment to the DETERRENT Act, which would require colleges to disclose certain gifts and contracts from foreign sources and bar contracts with some foreign countries and entities without a waiver. The amendment failed, 199 for and 214 against.

2025-8.name: Amtrak Executive Bonus Disclosure Act
2025-8.plain: The House voted 407 to 0 to pass a bill requiring Amtrak to publicly disclose the base pay and bonus pay of its executives in an annual report to Congress, including the criteria used to set bonuses, and to post that report on its website.

2025-80.name: DETERRENT Act Amendment on Foreign Gifts to Universities
2025-80.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the DETERRENT Act, a bill that would expand disclosure rules for universities receiving money or contracts from foreign sources. The amendment failed, with 92 in favor and 321 against.

2025-81.name: DETERRENT Act Amendment
2025-81.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the DETERRENT Act, a bill that would require colleges to report certain gifts and contracts from foreign sources and bar some contracts with foreign countries of concern without a waiver. The amendment was rejected, 3 in favor and 410 against.

2025-82.name: DETERRENT Act Amendment
2025-82.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the DETERRENT Act, which would require colleges to disclose certain gifts and contracts from foreign sources and bar certain foreign contracts without a waiver. The amendment was rejected, 4 in favor and 404 against.

2025-83.name: DETERRENT Act on Foreign Money at Colleges
2025-83.plain: The House voted 241 to 169 to pass the DETERRENT Act. It would require colleges to report certain gifts and contracts from foreign sources, including those tied to countries such as China and Russia, and could cut off federal student aid for violations.

2025-84.name: Tax Deadline Relief for Natural Disasters
2025-84.plain: The House passed a bill 388 to 0 that would let the IRS postpone federal tax deadlines for people affected by state-declared disasters when a governor requests it. It also extends the automatic tax deadline extension for disaster-affected taxpayers from 60 to 120 days.

2025-85.name: National Taxpayer Advocate Enhancement Act
2025-85.plain: The House passed this bill 385 to 0, with members of both parties voting yes and none voting no. It would let the National Taxpayer Advocate hire its own legal counsel to report directly to that office, and expand the advocate's authority over personnel in the Taxpayer Advocate Service, which helps taxpayers with IRS matters.

2025-86.name: Procedural Vote on Consumer Rules and Court Injunction and Voter Citizenship Bills
2025-86.plain: The House voted 215 to 213 to end debate and move toward final votes on several measures, including two resolutions opposing consumer finance rules and bills about court injunctions and proof of citizenship to register to vote. This vote was on how to proceed, not on the measures themselves.

2025-87.name: House Debate Rules for Five Measures
2025-87.plain: The House voted on the rules for debating five measures, including two consumer finance rules, limits on court injunctions, and proof of citizenship for voter registration. The rules were not approved, with 206 voting yes and 222 voting no.

2025-88.name: Disaster-Related Extension of Tax Deadlines
2025-88.plain: The House voted 423 to 0 to pass a bill requiring the IRS to treat tax deadlines postponed by federally declared disasters as extensions for calculating how far back a tax refund can reach, and to count those postponements for certain IRS notice deadlines.

2025-89.name: Vietnam Veterans Liver Fluke Cancer Study Act
2025-89.plain: The House voted 411 to 0 to pass a bill requiring the Department of Veterans Affairs to study how often bile duct cancer occurs among veterans who served in Vietnam, and to report on it to Congress.

2025-9.name: Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
2025-9.plain: The House passed this bill 405 to 5 under a fast-track process requiring two-thirds support. It would direct the Federal Emergency Management Agency to make information collection from disaster applicants less burdensome, convene a working group on damage assessments, and report to Congress.

2025-90.name: Clear Communication for Veterans Claims Act
2025-90.plain: The House voted 412 to 0 to pass the Clear Communication for Veterans Claims Act. It would have the Department of Veterans Affairs review the notices it sends to veterans applying for benefits, and it extends certain home loan fee rates through 2034.

2025-91.name: Procedural Vote on Rules for Five Measures
2025-91.plain: The House voted 213 to 211 to end debate and move ahead to final votes on a set of measures, including two consumer finance rules, a bill limiting court injunctions, and a bill requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote. This was a procedural step, not a vote on the measures themselves.

2025-92.name: House Debate Rules for Several Measures
2025-92.plain: The House voted 213 to 211 to approve the rules for debating several measures, including two consumer finance rules, a bill limiting court injunctions, and a bill requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote. This step only set how the debate would run; it did not itself decide those measures.

2025-93.name: Procedural Vote on Senate Budget Amendment
2025-93.plain: The House voted 217 to 212 to end debate and move to a final vote on a rule for considering the Senate's changes to a budget plan covering federal spending for 2025 and projected levels through 2034. This vote was procedural and did not decide the budget plan itself.

2025-94.name: Debate Rules for Congressional Budget Resolution
2025-94.plain: The House voted 216 to 215 to approve the rules for debating a Senate change to the federal budget plan for 2025 and later years. This was a procedural step that sets how the debate will run, not a final vote on the budget plan itself.

2025-95.name: Rule on Digital Payment App Oversight
2025-95.plain: The House voted 219 to 211 to pass a resolution that would cancel a federal consumer agency rule. The rule would have allowed the agency to oversee large nonbank payment apps, those handling at least 50 million transactions a year.

2025-96.name: Overdraft Fee Rule Repeal
2025-96.plain: The House voted 217 to 211 to pass a resolution that would cancel a federal rule limiting overdraft fees at very large banks. The rule required these banks to cap overdraft charges at $5, cap them higher with justification, or treat overdrafts as credit with required disclosures.

2025-97.name: Limits on Federal Court Nationwide Orders
2025-97.plain: The House rejected sending the No Rogue Rulings Act back to committee, by 212 votes to 217. The bill would bar federal district courts from issuing court orders that protect anyone beyond the parties in a particular case.

2025-98.name: No Rogue Rulings Act
2025-98.plain: The House passed the No Rogue Rulings Act by a vote of 219 to 213. The bill would bar federal district courts from issuing injunctions that reach beyond the parties in the specific case before them.

2025-99.name: Prioritizing Veterans' Survivors Act
2025-99.plain: The House voted 424 to 0 to pass a bill that would require the Office of Survivors Assistance to operate within the Office of the Secretary of Veterans Affairs instead of its current location within the Veterans Benefits Administration.

2026-10.name: Debate Rules for a Measure on Policy Priorities
2026-10.plain: The House voted 224 to 202 to approve the rules for debating another measure, H.R. 1834, which aims to advance policy priorities. This was a procedural step that sets how long debate lasts and which amendments are allowed, not a vote on the measure itself.

2026-100.name: Motion to Send DC Safety and Beautification Bill Back to Committee
2026-100.plain: The House voted on whether to send a bill back to committee before a final vote. The bill would set up a commission to advise on crime and immigration in Washington, D.C., and create a federal program to keep popular public areas clean and restore damaged monuments. The motion failed, 207 to 214.

2026-101.name: Making DC Safe and Beautiful Act
2026-101.plain: The House passed a bill, 218 to 206, that would create a federal commission to advise on crime and immigration enforcement in Washington, D.C., and a federal program to keep commonly visited areas there clean and maintained. The provisions end on January 2, 2029.

2026-102.name: Support for the Department of Homeland Security
2026-102.plain: The House voted 225 to 187 to approve a resolution expressing support for the Department of Homeland Security. It recognizes the importance of fully funding the department, warns that Americans face greater risk while it is subject to a funding lapse, and thanks its employees for their work.

2026-103.name: Pay Our Homeland Defenders Act Procedural Vote
2026-103.plain: The House voted 215 to 210 against sending the bill back to committee, so it moved on toward a final vote. The bill would provide funding to the Department of Homeland Security for the rest of 2026, end a partial shutdown that began February 14, 2026, and provide back pay to affected federal employees.

2026-104.name: Funding for Homeland Security Department
2026-104.plain: The House voted 218 to 206 to pass a bill that provides funding for the Department of Homeland Security for the rest of fiscal year 2026, ending a partial shutdown of the department that began February 14, 2026, and paying back wages to affected federal employees.

2026-105.name: Defending American Property Abroad Act
2026-105.plain: The House passed a bill, 247 to 164, that would let the President bar foreign ships from entering U.S. ports if they have stopped at a port in a Western Hemisphere country with a U.S. free trade agreement that seized American-owned property. The ban would end once the property is returned, fairly compensated, or the dispute is otherwise resolved.

2026-107.name: Procedural Vote on Consolidated Spending Bill
2026-107.plain: The House voted 209 to 206 to end debate and move to a final vote on whether to accept changes the Senate made to a bill that provides further funding for federal government operations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026. This was a procedural step, not the final vote on the measure itself.

2026-108.name: Procedural Resolution on Further Consolidated Appropriations
2026-108.plain: The House voted 213 to 203 to approve a resolution that sets the process for handling the Senate's changes to a spending bill that provides further funding for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026. Republicans voted yes and Democrats mostly voted no.

2026-109.name: Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act of 2025
2026-109.plain: The House voted 395 to 10 to pass a bill that would expand emergency payments to farmers and private forest owners after natural disasters, including advance payments for repairing or replacing farm structures and fencing. Wildfire damage caused by natural spread would also be eligible.

2026-11.name: Bill to Advance Policy Priorities
2026-11.plain: The House voted 230 to 196 to pass a bill described as advancing policy priorities to break gridlock. The official facts do not say what specific changes it would make.

2026-110.name: ALERT Act: Aircraft Tracking and Safety
2026-110.plain: The House passed the ALERT Act by 396 votes to 10 under a fast-track process. The bill would require military and civilian aircraft to carry improved tracking and communication equipment (ADS-B In) by 2031, and expand aviation safety oversight.

2026-111.name: Procedural Vote on Four Clean Air and Tax Measures
2026-111.plain: The House voted 212 to 211 to end debate and move to a final vote on a package of four measures: three bills amending the Clean Air Act and a resolution supporting tax policies for working families. This was a procedural vote, not a vote on the measures themselves.

2026-112.name: Debate Rules for Clean Air and Tax Measures
2026-112.plain: The House voted 214 to 212 to approve the rules for debating several measures on Clean Air Act changes, foreign emissions standards, and a resolution supporting tax policies for working families. The vote set how long debate would last and which changes could be offered; it did not itself change any law.

2026-113.name: Bringing Haiti Temporary Protected Status Bill to Floor
2026-113.plain: The House voted 219 to 209 to bring a bill to the floor for debate that would require the Homeland Security Secretary to designate Haiti for temporary protected status. Under this vote, the House chose to move the measure out of committee.

2026-114.name: Removing Forces from Hostilities with Iran
2026-114.plain: The House voted on a resolution directing the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress or a declaration of war authorizes them, with exceptions for defending the U.S., an ally, or a partner from imminent attack. The resolution failed, 213 in favor to 214 against.

2026-115.name: Motion to Send FENCES Act Back to Committee
2026-115.plain: The House rejected a motion to send the FENCES Act back to committee, so the bill moved on toward a final vote. The bill would exempt states from Clean Air Act penalties for pollution coming from outside their control, such as wildfire smoke or emissions from other countries.

2026-116.name: FENCES Act: Clean Air Penalty Exemptions
2026-116.plain: The House voted 220 to 208 to pass the FENCES Act. It would exempt states from Clean Air Act penalties for pollution they cannot control, such as smoke from wildfires or emissions from other countries.

2026-117.name: RED Tape Act Motion to Recommit
2026-117.plain: The House voted 213 to 216 against sending the RED Tape Act back to committee, so the bill moved on to its final vote. The bill would remove a requirement that the EPA review and comment on federal construction projects and major federal actions that already undergo environmental review under NEPA.

2026-118.name: RED Tape Act on Environmental Reviews
2026-118.plain: The House passed the RED Tape Act, 222 to 205. The bill would remove a requirement that the Environmental Protection Agency review and comment on federal construction projects and other major federal actions that already undergo a separate environmental review.

2026-119.name: Debate Rules for Haiti Protected Status Bill
2026-119.plain: The House voted 220 to 207 to approve the rules for debating a bill that would require the Homeland Security Secretary to grant temporary protected status to Haiti. This was a procedural step that sets how the debate on that bill will run, not a vote on the bill itself.

2026-12.name: Affordable HOMES Act
2026-12.plain: The House passed the Affordable HOMES Act, 263 to 147. The bill cancels a 2022 Energy Department rule setting energy efficiency standards for manufactured homes and removes the department's power to issue similar rules.

2026-120.name: Temporary Protected Status for Haiti
2026-120.plain: The House voted 224 to 204 to pass a bill directing the Department of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status for 18 months starting August 3, 2025. That status would allow eligible Haitian nationals to obtain work authorization, protect them from detention based on immigration status, and shield them from removal while they keep the status.

2026-121.name: Resolution Supporting Tax Policies for Working Families
2026-121.plain: The House voted 219 to 207 to approve a resolution expressing support for tax policies that help working families and recognizing tax relief enacted in 2025. Nearly all Republicans voted yes, and nearly all Democrats voted no.

2026-122.name: Rule for Debate on Surveillance Law Extension
2026-122.plain: The House voted 211 to 210 to end debate and move to a final vote on whether to extend certain surveillance authorities through October 20, 2027. This was a procedural step, not a vote on the extension itself.

2026-123.name: Extending Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Authority
2026-123.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to a bill that would extend certain foreign intelligence surveillance powers through October 20, 2027. The amendment failed, 200 to 220.

2026-124.name: Debate Rules for Foreign Surveillance Extension
2026-124.plain: The House voted on the rules for debating a bill to extend certain foreign intelligence surveillance powers to October 2027. The rules failed, 197 in favor to 228 against, so the proposal to move ahead was rejected.

2026-125.name: Expediting Federal Broadband Deployment Reviews Act
2026-125.plain: The House voted 384 to 9 to pass a bill creating a government task force to speed up federal reviews of requests to build or change communications facilities on public lands. The task force would set review goals, monitor agencies, and report to Congress on its work.

2026-126.name: Emergency Reporting Act
2026-126.plain: The House voted to pass the Emergency Reporting Act, 386 to 7. It would require the Federal Communications Commission to study 9-1-1 phone outages, hold yearly public hearings after long communications outages during disasters, and publish reports with recommendations for improving communications reliability.

2026-127.name: Kari's Law Reporting Act
2026-127.plain: The House voted 405 to 5 to pass a bill requiring the Federal Communications Commission to publish a report on how well manufacturers and vendors of multiline phone systems have complied with Kari's Law, which lets people dial 9-1-1 directly without an extra prefix, and to recommend any needed improvements.

2026-128.name: Rural Health Care Grants Reauthorization
2026-128.plain: The House voted 406 to 4 to pass a bill extending through 2030 federal grant programs that fund health care services, networks, and small providers in rural areas. The bill also requires that grant money be used to serve underserved groups and involve them in planning.

2026-129.name: Hydropower Project Construction Deadline Extensions
2026-129.plain: The House passed a bill, 394 to 14, that would let federal regulators extend construction deadlines for certain hydropower projects licensed before March 13, 2020. Regulators could grant up to six more years beyond current law, and could reinstate some expired licenses.

2026-13.name: Remote Access Security Act
2026-13.plain: The House passed the Remote Access Security Act, 369 to 22. The bill would extend U.S. export controls to foreign people who remotely use controlled items, such as through the internet or cloud computing, and let the Commerce Department issue licenses and impose penalties for that access.

2026-130.name: Rule Vote on Energy, Endangered Species, and Geothermal Bills
2026-130.plain: The House voted 180 to 179 to end debate and move toward a final vote on three bills: one on federal building energy standards, one on the Endangered Species Act, and one on geothermal drilling permits. The vote was on how the bills would be considered, not on the bills themselves.

2026-131.name: Debate Rules for Three Environmental and Energy Bills
2026-131.plain: The House voted 211 to 206 to approve the rules for debating three bills: one repealing federal building energy efficiency standards, one changing the Endangered Species Act, and one waiving a federal drilling permit for certain geothermal activities. The vote set how long debate would last and which amendments were allowed, but did not itself decide those bills.

2026-132.name: Support for Rural Communities
2026-132.plain: The House voted 220 to 196 to approve a resolution expressing support for rural communities across the United States, and recognizing the House's work in backing them on energy, health care, manufacturing, and broadband.

2026-133.name: Federal Building Energy Efficiency Standards Repeal
2026-133.plain: The House voted on whether to send the Reliable Federal Infrastructure Act back to committee, and the motion failed 203 to 214. The bill would repeal energy efficiency standards that phase out fossil fuel use in new federal buildings and major renovations by 2030.

2026-134.name: Reliable Federal Infrastructure Act
2026-134.plain: The House voted 215 to 202 to pass the Reliable Federal Infrastructure Act. It would repeal energy efficiency rules that phased out fossil fuel use in new federal buildings and major renovations by 2030, and it would stop certain green building certification systems from denying federal buildings certification based solely on fossil fuel use.

2026-135.name: FIRE Act Motion to Recommit
2026-135.plain: The House voted on whether to send the FIRE Act back to committee before a final vote. The motion failed, 206 to 214, so the bill moved on toward a final vote. The bill would change how air pollution rules treat wildfire-related events and require the EPA to revise its regulations on them.

2026-136.name: FIRE Act on Wildfire Air Pollution Rules
2026-136.plain: The House passed the FIRE Act, 220 to 198. The bill changes how the EPA treats air pollution data affected by wildfires and wildfire-prevention work, including rules for certain high-temperature and dry-weather events.

2026-137.name: HEATS Act on Geothermal Energy Permits
2026-137.plain: The House passed the HEATS Act, 231 to 186, which would exempt certain geothermal energy drilling on state and private lands from federal drilling permits and from federal environmental and historic preservation reviews.

2026-138.name: IRS Whistleblower Program Improvement Act
2026-138.plain: The House voted to pass a bill changing how IRS whistleblower awards are reviewed, lets whistleblowers stay anonymous in Tax Court cases, and adds interest to late awards and deductions for attorney fees. It passed 346 to 10.

2026-139.name: Clergy Social Security and Medicare Opt-Back-In Act
2026-139.plain: The House passed a bill, 350 to 5, that gives clergy members who opted out of Social Security and Medicare taxes for religious reasons a two-year window to opt back in. Once they revoke their exemption, the choice is permanent.

2026-14.name: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
2026-14.plain: The House passed this bill, 340 to 54, to keep federal agencies funded at current levels through December 11, 2026, so a shutdown is avoided, and to extend several expiring programs, including grain inspection, cybersecurity information sharing, and trade benefits for African countries.

2026-140.name: Procedural Vote on Five Bills and a Budget Resolution
2026-140.plain: The House voted 215 to 210 to end debate and move to a final vote on a package that includes a farm bill, a school gender-marker parental consent bill, a 2026 budget resolution, a Jewish servicemember burial marker bill, and an ethanol fuel waiver bill. This vote was not on those measures themselves.

2026-141.name: House Rules for Debating Several Bills
2026-141.plain: The House voted 216 to 210 to approve rules for debating several separate measures, including farm programs, school gender-marker consent, the federal budget, and others. This was a procedural step that sets how long debate lasts and which amendments are allowed, not a final vote on those measures.

2026-142.name: Foreign Intelligence Surveillance and Central Bank Digital Currency Bill
2026-142.plain: The House passed the bill 235 to 191. It would extend a foreign intelligence surveillance law to April 30, 2029, add new limits on how the FBI searches collected communications of U.S. persons, and bar the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency.

2026-143.name: Federal Budget Resolution for Fiscal Year 2026
2026-143.plain: The House approved a budget plan for the federal government for 2026, with 2027 through 2035 targets, by 215 to 211. The plan includes instructions for future legislation that could add up to $70 billion to the deficit.

2026-144.name: Amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
2026-144.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the farm bill, which covers farm programs, nutrition assistance, conservation, and crop insurance. The amendment failed, 210 in favor to 216 against, so it was not added to the bill.

2026-145.name: Amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
2026-145.plain: The House voted 384 to 35 to adopt an amendment changing the farm bill, which covers Department of Agriculture programs on crops, conservation, trade, nutrition, farm credit, rural development, research, forestry, energy, crop insurance, livestock, and foreign purchases of U.S. farmland.

2026-146.name: Farm Bill Amendment
2026-146.plain: The House voted 416 to 8 to add an amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, which reauthorizes Department of Agriculture programs through 2031, covering areas such as farm support, conservation, nutrition assistance, and crop insurance.

2026-147.name: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 Amendment
2026-147.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, which covers Department of Agriculture programs such as farm support, conservation, nutrition assistance, and crop insurance. The amendment failed, with 69 voting yes and 355 voting no.

2026-148.name: Amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
2026-148.plain: The House voted 280 to 142 to add an amendment to the farm bill, which covers Department of Agriculture programs such as crop support, conservation, nutrition assistance, rural development, and crop insurance. The bill itself would reauthorize these programs through 2031.

2026-149.name: Amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026
2026-149.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, which would update Department of Agriculture programs covering farm support, conservation, nutrition, and crop insurance. The amendment failed, 187 in favor to 239 against.

2026-15.name: Haiti Economic Lift Program Extension
2026-15.plain: The House voted 345 to 45 to pass a bill extending through 2028 the duty-free tariff rules for certain apparel imported from Haiti. It also directs refunds of duties paid on such imports entered after September 30, 2025.

2026-150.name: Amendment to the Farm Bill
2026-150.plain: The House voted 233 to 194 to add an amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, a bill covering farm programs, food assistance, and related Agriculture Department policies. Most Democrats voted yes, and most Republicans voted no.

2026-151.name: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 Amendment
2026-151.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the farm bill, which covers farm programs, conservation, nutrition assistance, crop insurance, and rural development. The amendment was rejected, 186 in favor to 238 against.

2026-152.name: Farm Bill Amendment
2026-152.plain: The House voted 215 to 213 to add an amendment to the farm bill, which renews Department of Agriculture programs covering crop support, conservation, nutrition assistance, rural development, crop insurance, and foreign ownership of U.S. farmland through 2031.

2026-153.name: Farm Bill Sent Back to Committee
2026-153.plain: The House voted on whether to send the farm bill back to committee for more work, rather than moving to a final vote. The motion failed 211 to 214, so the bill moved on to the final vote. The bill would reauthorize and modify Department of Agriculture programs covering crop support, conservation, nutrition assistance, rural development, and crop insurance through 2031.

2026-154.name: Farm Bill
2026-154.plain: The House passed the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 by 224 to 200. The bill renews and changes Department of Agriculture programs through 2031, covering areas such as farm support, conservation, nutrition assistance, crop insurance, and rural development.

2026-155.name: Extension of Foreign Surveillance Authorities
2026-155.plain: The House passed a bill extending for a period of time certain authorities for surveillance of communications of people believed to be outside the United States, to gather foreign intelligence. The vote was 261 in favor and 111 against, and the bill had to pass with two-thirds support under a fast-track process.

2026-156.name: Save Our Shrimpers Act
2026-156.plain: The House passed the Save Our Shrimpers Act, 391 to 18. The bill would bar federal money from going to international lending institutions for financing shrimp farming, shrimp processing, or shrimp exports abroad, and would require a yearly government report on compliance.

2026-157.name: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act
2026-157.plain: The House passed the bill 348 to 60. It expands federal prosecution of organized theft from stores and shipments, lets authorities seize related proceeds, adds gift cards to money laundering law, and temporarily creates a Homeland Security coordination center for these crimes.

2026-158.name: Rule Setting Debate on Five Bills
2026-158.plain: The House voted 211 to 208 to pass a procedural rule that sets the terms for debating five bills, covering cashless bail, bail fraud, court monitors, support for law enforcement, and military construction and veterans spending. The vote was to end debate on the rule, not a vote on the bills themselves.

2026-159.name: Debate Rules for Five House Bills
2026-159.plain: The House voted 214 to 208 to approve the rules for debating five measures, including bills on cashless bail, bail fraud, court monitors, support for law enforcement, and military construction and veterans spending. This was a procedural step that sets how debate on those measures will proceed.

2026-16.name: Procedural Vote on Five Labor and Retirement Bills
2026-16.plain: The House voted 206 to 205 to end debate and move to a final vote on a package of five bills concerning retirement plans, overtime pay, tipped workers, and joint employers. This was a procedural vote, not a vote on the bills themselves.

2026-160.name: Ending Debate on Farm Bill Procedures
2026-160.plain: The House voted 211 to 206 to end debate and move to a final vote on a procedural measure. The measure would remove a requirement to include the text of a separate fuel retailer bill within the farm bill, H.R. 7567. This was not the final vote on the farm bill itself.

2026-161.name: Removing Text Requirement from Farm Bill Rule
2026-161.plain: The House approved a resolution that removes a requirement to include a separate fuel and retail choice bill's text within the farm bill, by a vote of 213 to 208.

2026-162.name: Resolution Honoring Fallen Law Enforcement Officers
2026-162.plain: The House approved a resolution expressing support for police and other law enforcement officers, recognizing their sacrifice, and offering condolences to the families of officers killed in the line of duty. The vote was 418 in favor and 2 against.

2026-163.name: Motion to Send Ethanol Fuel Bill Back to Committee
2026-163.plain: The House voted on whether to send the bill allowing gasoline with up to 15% ethanol to be sold year-round back to committee. The motion failed, 112 to 309, so the bill moved on toward a final vote.

2026-164.name: Year-Round Sale of E15 Gasoline
2026-164.plain: The House voted 218 to 203 to pass a bill that would let gasoline blended with up to 15% ethanol be sold year-round, and would change a renewable fuel program so small refineries can get compliance credits back in some cases.

2026-165.name: Support for Law Enforcement Officers
2026-165.plain: The House voted 243 to 173 to approve a resolution expressing support for law enforcement officers and recognizing their contributions and sacrifices. Republicans voted in favor, and Democrats were divided, with 29 for it and 173 against it.

2026-166.name: Resolution Countering Antisemitism
2026-166.plain: The House voted 419 to 0 to approve a resolution calling on elected officials, faith leaders, and civil society leaders to condemn and counter antisemitism. It also honors the contributions of Jewish-American servicemembers and commits to ensuring all Americans can worship without fear of violence or persecution.

2026-167.name: Urging Release of Detained Activists and Pastors in China
2026-167.plain: The House voted 414 to 0 to approve a non-binding resolution asking the President to prioritize the release of five people detained by China, including pastors and Jimmy Lai, during future meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping, and to seek proof of life, legal counsel, family contact and medical care for them.

2026-168.name: Bill on Bail Bonds and Insurance Fraud
2026-168.plain: The House voted 210 to 213 against sending the bill back to committee, so the bill moved on toward a final vote. The bill would treat paying bail or bail bonds as insurance business under federal law, which would make it subject to federal insurance-fraud rules.

2026-169.name: Keeping Violent Offenders Off Our Streets Act
2026-169.plain: The House passed a bill, 243 to 179, that would count bail payments, including cash bail from charitable bail funds, as the business of insurance under federal law, making such payments subject to federal insurance fraud crimes and state insurance licensing and regulation.

2026-17.name: Debate Rules for Five Workplace and Retirement Bills
2026-17.plain: The House voted 214 to 207 to approve the rules for debating five bills on retirement plans, overtime, tipped workers, and joint employers. This was a procedural step that sets how long debate lasts and which changes may be offered, not a final vote on the bills themselves.

2026-170.name: War Powers Resolution on Iran Hostilities
2026-170.plain: The House voted on a resolution directing the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran by March 30, 2026, unless Congress has authorized the action. The measure failed on a 212-212 tie, so it was not approved.

2026-171.name: Cashless Bail Reporting Act
2026-171.plain: The House voted 308 to 116 to pass the Cashless Bail Reporting Act. It would require the Justice Department to publish a yearly list of state and local governments that allow people charged with certain serious crimes, such as burglary, murder, rape, looting or vandalism, to be released before trial without cash bail.

2026-172.name: Monitor Accountability Act: Send Back to Committee
2026-172.plain: The House voted 210 to 213 against sending the Monitor Accountability Act back to committee, so the bill moved on toward a final vote. The bill would set rules for independent monitors who oversee state and local governments under court settlements, including public comment before appointment, a five-year term limit, and caps on fees.

2026-173.name: Monitor Accountability Act
2026-173.plain: The House passed the Monitor Accountability Act, 219 to 204. The bill would require courts to set conditions on appointing independent monitors who oversee local and state governments under court settlements, including public notice and comment, a five-year term limit, public reporting of fees, and a fee cap.

2026-174.name: Amendment to Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Spending Bill
2026-174.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the bill that provides funding for military construction, Department of Veterans Affairs programs, and related agencies for fiscal year 2027. The amendment was rejected, 80 in favor and 333 against.

2026-175.name: Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Funding Bill
2026-175.plain: The House passed a bill providing money for military construction, Department of Veterans Affairs programs, and related agencies for the 2027 fiscal year, by a vote of 400 to 15.

2026-176.name: Procedural Resolution on H.R. 6644 Senate Amendment
2026-176.plain: The House voted 396 to 13 to approve a resolution that accepts changes the Senate made to a bill, using a fast-track process requiring two-thirds support. The official facts do not describe what the bill would do.

2026-177.name: Keeping Deposits Local Act
2026-177.plain: The House passed the Keeping Deposits Local Act, 405 to 0. The bill would raise the amount banks can accept as reciprocal deposits, set that limit based on each bank's total liabilities, and let banks rated 1, 2, or 3 under the CAMELS scale qualify.

2026-178.name: American Access to Banking Act
2026-178.plain: The House passed the American Access to Banking Act, 405 to 4. It would require federal financial regulators to review and simplify how new banks and credit unions apply to open, assign applicants a caseworker on request, and set up outreach plans to help applicants understand the process.

2026-179.name: Community Bank Deposit Access Act
2026-179.plain: The House passed a bill, 393 to 16, that would stop treating certain custodial deposits at smaller community banks as brokered deposits, so those banks face less additional oversight. The bill also applies existing interest rate limits to similar banks that accept these deposits.

2026-18.name: Voluntary Training and Work Hours Bill
2026-18.plain: The House voted 209 to 213 against sending this bill back to committee, so it moved on toward a final vote. The bill would exclude certain voluntary employer training held outside regular working hours from counting as paid work hours, as long as choosing not to take part doesn't hurt the worker's conditions and no work is done during the training.

2026-180.name: Veterans Medical Facility Project in St. Louis
2026-180.plain: The House voted 405 to 5 to pass a bill authorizing the Department of Veterans Affairs to carry out a major medical facility project in St. Louis, Missouri, during fiscal year 2026. The project includes a new bed tower, clinical expansion, administrative building, warehouse, utility plant, and parking garages, with a maximum spending limit set by the bill.

2026-181.name: Lulu's Law: Shark Attack Emergency Alerts
2026-181.plain: The House passed Lulu's Law by 401 votes to 6. The bill would require the Federal Communications Commission to issue an order allowing emergency alerts to be sent to mobile phones when a shark attack occurs.

2026-182.name: 25th Anniversary of 9/11 Commemorative Coin Act
2026-182.plain: The House passed the bill 415 to 0. It directs the Treasury to mint coins marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 attacks and the National September 11 Memorial and Museum, with some sales money going to the museum's upkeep.

2026-183.name: Stopping Indoctrination and Protecting Kids Act
2026-183.plain: The House voted on whether to send the bill back to committee before a final vote, and the attempt failed 207 to 208. The bill would require public elementary and middle schools to get parental consent before changing a student's gender on school forms or sex-based accommodations such as bathrooms or locker rooms, as a condition of receiving certain federal school funds.

2026-184.name: Stopping Indoctrination and Protecting Kids Act
2026-184.plain: The House passed the bill 217 to 198. It would require public elementary and middle schools to get parental consent before changing a student's gender markers, pronouns, or preferred name on school forms, or changing sex-based accommodations such as locker rooms or bathrooms, in order to keep certain federal education funds.

2026-185.name: Procedural Vote on Veterans and Smithsonian Bills
2026-185.plain: The House voted 209 to 207 to end debate and move to a final vote on a package of three bills and a related rule. The package covers limits on sharing certain veterans' information for gun background checks, increases to disability and survivor payments for veterans, and allowing a Smithsonian women's history museum on the National Mall.

2026-186.name: Debate Rules for Three Bills
2026-186.plain: The House voted 208 to 207 to approve the rules for debating three measures: one on veterans' records and background checks, one on raising veterans' disability payments, and one on a women's history museum on the National Mall. This was a procedural step that sets how the debate will run, not a vote on the measures themselves.

2026-187.name: Smithsonian American Women's History Museum Act
2026-187.plain: The House voted on whether to send the bill back to committee, and the motion failed 209 to 209, so the bill moved on. The bill would authorize a Smithsonian American Women's History Museum on a site on the National Mall and limit it to the history of biological women.

2026-188.name: Smithsonian American Women's History Museum Act
2026-188.plain: The House voted on whether to pass a bill to create a Smithsonian museum on women's history in the United States on a site near the National Mall, limited to the history of biological women. The bill failed, 204 in favor to 216 against.

2026-189.name: Veterans Gun Rights Bill Sent Back to Committee
2026-189.plain: The House voted 208 to 210 on whether to send the Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act back to committee, and the motion failed. The bill would stop the Department of Veterans Affairs from sending veterans' personal information to the national gun background check system just because they have a fiduciary who manages their benefits, unless a judge finds them a danger to themselves or others.

2026-19.name: Flexibility for Workers Education Act
2026-19.plain: The House voted on whether to pass a bill that would exclude voluntary training held outside regular working hours from counting as hours worked under federal wage law, if employees who skip it face no penalty and do no work during it. The bill failed, 209 in favor to 215 against.

2026-190.name: Veterans Firearm Background Check Privacy Bill
2026-190.plain: The House passed a bill, 216 to 201, that would stop the Department of Veterans Affairs from sending veterans' personal information to the national gun background check system just because they have a fiduciary managing their benefits, unless a court finds they pose a danger to themselves or others.

2026-191.name: Veterans Benefits Expansion Act of 2026
2026-191.plain: The House passed this bill 235 to 179. It would add a monthly allowance for certain disabled veterans who already receive aid-and-attendance benefits, raise survivor payments (DIC), and expand VA home loan eligibility for some reserve and National Guard members.

2026-192.name: American Battlefield Protection Program Amendments Act
2026-192.plain: The House passed a bill, 404 to 13, that extends through 2036 three National Park Service grant programs for acquiring, restoring and modernizing the interpretation of certain U.S. battlefields, and requires studies of French and Indian War and Mexican-American War sites for possible preservation.

2026-193.name: ARTIST Act on Alaska Native Marine Mammal Products
2026-193.plain: The House passed the ARTIST Act, 404 to 14, with a fast-track process requiring two-thirds support. The bill would stop states from banning marine mammal ivory, bone, or baleen legally made by Alaska Natives as authentic handicrafts and clothing, including their sale and trade across state lines.

2026-194.name: Procedural Vote on Four Spending and Program Bills
2026-194.plain: The House voted 208 to 207 to pass a procedural step that ends debate and moves the House toward a final vote on four bills. The bills cover agriculture and food programs, child care funding for noncompliant states, identity fraud checks on student aid forms, and temporary assistance for needy families. Republicans voted yes and Democrats voted no.

2026-195.name: Debate Rules for Four Bills
2026-195.plain: The House voted 211 to 207 to approve the rules for debating four bills: one on agriculture and FDA spending, one on child care funding for noncompliant states, one on identity fraud checks for student aid forms, and one on fraud and improper payments in temporary assistance for needy families. This was a procedural step, not a vote on the bills themselves.

2026-196.name: Northwest Straits Marine Conservation Initiative Reauthorization Act
2026-196.plain: The House voted 374 to 49 to pass a bill extending for seven years a program that works to protect and restore marine waters, habitats and species in the Northwest Straits region of Washington state. The bill was passed under a fast-track process requiring two-thirds support.

2026-197.name: Child Care Program Sanctions Bill
2026-197.plain: The House voted on whether to send the bill back to committee, and the motion failed 210 to 213. The bill would require federal sanctions, including disqualifying a state from receiving child care block grant funds, when a state substantially violates program rules.

2026-198.name: Child Care Program Sanctions for Repeat Violations
2026-198.plain: The House voted 217 to 207 to pass a bill requiring federal sanctions, including disqualifying a state from funds, when a state substantially fails to follow the rules of the Child Care and Development Block Grant program. Currently such sanctions are optional.

2026-199.name: Directing Removal of U.S. Forces from Hostilities with Iran
